definition_zh: 熔化的；（金属、岩石）熔融的；浇铸成的
definition_en: made liquid by great heat, especially metal or rock; shaped by being poured while melted
core_image: 炉口倾出的铁水在砂模沟槽里铺开，暗红的光顺槽流动，冷却后凝成一块硬物
scene: 铸工打开炉门，橙红色的金属液顺着沟槽流进砂模，空气里全是热浪。The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
sceneCN: 这里 molten 指「经高温熔化后呈液态的」（第 1 个义项：因高热熔成液体，多指金属或岩石）；句意为熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满砂模。可辨识物件：炉门、铁水沟槽、砂模、热浪。

pos.zh: 熔化的；熔融的；浇铸成的
melt 的过去分词（古旧或方言用法，表示已熔化）

derivatives.zh: 熔化；融化的；令人怜惜的

senses.title: Metal made liquid by heat
senses.definition: of metal: melted and still liquid because of intense heat
senses.definitionCN: 指金属因高温熔化而处于液态
senses.example: The molten iron ran along the channel and filled the sand mould.
senses.exampleCN: 熔化的铁水沿沟槽流下，灌满了砂模。
senses.why: molten is the old past participle of melt, and -en in broken, frozen and spoken marks a finished state, so the word describes metal that has already been liquefied, not metal that is melting now.
senses.whyCN: molten 是 melt 的古老过去分词，而 broken、frozen、spoken 中的 -en 都标记完成状态，因此这个词说的是「已经熔成液体」的金属，而不是「正在熔化」的金属。

senses.title: Rock melted underground
senses.titleCN: 地下的岩石呈熔融状态
senses.definition: of rock: liquefied by the heat of the earth, as in magma below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石因地热而熔化，如地表之下的岩浆
senses.example: Molten rock rises through cracks in the crust and feeds the volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 熔融的岩石沿地壳裂缝上升，为火山提供物质。
senses.why: the geological sense keeps the same picture but moves it underground, where pressure and heat hold rock in a liquid state that would freeze at the surface.
senses.whyCN: 地质义沿用同一幅图景，只是把它移到地下：在高压与高温下，岩石保持液态，一旦到地表就会凝固。

senses.title: Glass or other material in a furnace
senses.titleCN: 玻璃等材料在炉中熔成液态
senses.definition: of glass, wax or similar material: reduced to liquid in a furnace or crucible
senses.definitionCN: 指玻璃、蜡等材料在炉或坩埚中熔成液体
senses.example: Workers poured the molten glass into a long iron trough.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把熔融的玻璃倒进一条长铁槽。
senses.why: the participle was never limited to metals; any solid that heat turns into a pourable liquid can be called molten, and glass-making fixed the word in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词从来不限于金属；任何被高温变成可倾倒液体的固体都可以叫 molten，制玻璃的工艺把这一义项固定下来。

senses.title: Glowing with heat
senses.definition: so hot that the material glows red, orange or white
senses.definitionCN: 指温度高到发出红、橙或白色光
senses.example: The molten core of the furnace lit the whole workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 炉膛里熔融的核心照亮了整个车间。
senses.why: a liquid at such temperatures radiates visible light, so molten naturally extends from 'liquid by heat' to 'glowing because of heat'.
senses.whyCN: 处于这种温度的液体会辐射可见光，因此 molten 从「因热成液」自然延伸到「因热发光」。

senses.title: Cast from melted material
senses.titleCN: 用熔化的材料浇铸成型
senses.definition: formed by pouring melted material into a mould and letting it harden
senses.definitionCN: 指把熔化的材料倒入模具、冷却硬化而成形
senses.example: A molten bronze horse was cast in a single pour.
senses.exampleCN: 一匹熔铜的马在一次浇铸中成型。
senses.why: casting is the practical use of the participle: the material is molten at the moment of the pour, and the shape it takes is the shape of the mould.
senses.whyCN: 浇铸是这个分词的实际用途：材料在倾倒的一刻是熔融的，它得到的形状就是模具的形状。

senses.title: High-temperature liquid in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学中的高温熔融体系
senses.definition: of a salt or reagent: melted and used as a liquid medium at high temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指盐或试剂在高温下熔成液体并作为反应介质
senses.example: Molten salt stores heat in the plant's thermal tanks.
senses.exampleCN: 熔盐在电厂的热罐中储存热量。
senses.why: in industrial chemistry the participle becomes a technical label: a molten salt is a liquid ionic medium, not water-based and not a solution.
senses.whyCN: 在工业化学中，这个分词成了技术标签：熔盐是液态离子介质，既不是水溶液，也不是溶剂中的溶液。

senses.title: Flowing light or colour in description
senses.titleCN: 描写中流动的光或色彩
senses.definition: literary: of light or colour, glowing and fluid as if poured
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：指光或色彩如被倾倒般流动、灼亮
senses.example: The molten gold of sunset spilled across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 落日熔金般的光铺满海湾。
senses.why: the image of poured metal gives writers a way to describe light that seems liquid, and this figurative use keeps the heat and the flow of the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 「倾倒金属」的形象给写作者提供了描写看似液态的光的办法，这一比喻义保留了原图景中的高温与流动。

senses.title: Intense, barely contained feeling
senses.titleCN: 强烈而几乎压不住的情绪
senses.definition: figurative: of anger, energy or passion, so intense that it seems to burn and flow
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：指愤怒、能量或激情强烈到仿佛在燃烧、流动
senses.example: Her molten anger frightened everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她如熔岩般的怒火让屋里所有人都害怕。
senses.why: heat and loss of shape are the two parts of the image, and both transfer to emotion: something solid has become dangerous, moving and hot.
senses.whyCN: 高温与失去形状是这幅图景的两个部分，两者都能转移到情绪上：原本稳固的东西变得危险、流动而灼热。

intro.en: Molten is the old past participle of the English verb melt, and its history is the history of that verb rather than of a Latin borrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molten 是英语动词 melt 的古老过去分词，它的历史就是 melt 这个词的历史，而不是一次拉丁语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Meltan meant 'to melt, become liquid, dissolve' and also 'to digest' in the bodily sense; the verb is recorded in Old English before the Norman period.
items.cn: meltan 意为「熔化、变成液体、溶解」，也指身体意义上的「消化」；这个词在诺曼征服之前的古英语中已有记录。

items.en: *Meltanan is a reconstruction supported by Old Norse melta and Old High German smelzan 'to melt'; no single attested form of the root survives outside the Germanic group.
items.cn: *meltanan 是重构形式，依据古诺斯语 melta 与古高地德语 smelzan「熔化」；这个词根在日耳曼语族之外没有留存下来的单一形式。

items.en: The ending -en marks a completed state in strong past participles such as broken, frozen, spoken and molten, so the form says 'already melted' rather than 'melting'.
items.cn: 后缀 -en 在 broken、frozen、spoken、molten 这类强变化过去分词中标记完成状态，因此这一形式说的是「已经熔化」，而不是「正在熔化」。

items.en: In Middle English molten is recorded of liquefied metal, wax and ore, usually in the phrase 'molten lead' or 'molten metal'.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，molten 已用于熔化的金属、蜡与矿石，常见于「熔铅」「熔融金属」这类说法。

items.en: From the seventeenth century metallurgy fixed the word in phrases such as molten iron, and geology later applied it to magma and lava; the technical senses keep the participle's perfect meaning.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，冶金学用 molten iron（铁水）这类说法把词固定下来，地质学后来把它用于岩浆与熔岩；这些技术义都保留了分词的完成意味。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic history of *meltanan is unsettled, and the old comparison with Latin mollis 'soft' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation; any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：*meltanan 在日耳曼语之前的历史没有定论，把它与拉丁 mollis「软」相比只是假说，并非已证实的派生；凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound like molten but come from other roots; group two collects words for the same physical state of matter.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音近似但词根不同的词；第二组是描述同一物态的词。

entries.definition: Means to shed feathers, hair or skin, and comes from a separate Germanic and Old French line; the resemblance to molten is only in sound and spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为脱换羽毛、毛发或外皮，来自另一条日耳曼语与古法语线索；与 molten 的相似只在音形。

entries.definition: To extract metal from ore by heating, from Middle Dutch smelten 'to melt'; it is a Germanic relative of melt rather than a form of molten itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指加热矿石以提炼金属，来自中古荷兰语 smelten「熔化」；它是 melt 在日耳曼语中的亲属，而不是 molten 本身的一个形式。

entries.definition: A hollow form for casting, or the verb to shape something; it goes back through Old French to Latin modulus 'small measure', so it is not related to melt at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指浇铸用的凹型，或「塑造」这一动词；它经古法语上溯到拉丁 modulus「小量度」，与 melt 毫无词源关系。

entries.definition: The regular past participle of melt, used for anything that has melted, from butter to snow; molten is the older form and today mostly describes metal, rock and glass.
entries.definitionCN: melt 的规则过去分词，可用于黄油、积雪等任何融化之物；molten 是较早的形式，今天多用于金属、岩石与玻璃。

entries.definition: A formal or technical word for turning a solid into a liquid, from Latin liquere 'be fluid'; it states the result without the image of a furnace.
entries.definitionCN: 使固体变成液体的正式或技术用词，来自拉丁 liquere「呈液态」；它只陈述结果，不带炉火的形象。

entries.definition: Describes an object glowing with heat, from Latin candere 'to shine'; it names the light rather than the liquid state that molten includes.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体因高温而发光，来自拉丁 candere「发光」；它命名的是光，而 molten 还包含液态这一层。

entries.definition: Means melted together into one mass, from Latin fundere 'to pour'; it stresses union, where molten stresses the liquid condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指经热熔合为一体，来自拉丁 fundere「倾倒」；它强调结合，molten 强调液态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle ending, the real word family and the fixed technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词后缀、真实的词族与固定技术搭配。

normal.en: Melt plus -en: the same ending as in broken, frozen and spoken, all marking a finished state.
normal.cn: melt 加 -en：与 broken、frozen、spoken 同一个后缀，都标记完成状态。

normal.en: The family runs melt, melting, melted, meltwater, meltdown, remelt.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 melt、melting、melted、meltwater、meltdown、remelt。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the sense: molten metal, molten rock, molten glass, molten salt.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载词义：熔融金属、熔融岩石、熔融玻璃、熔盐。

normal.en: In geology the word pairs with magma below ground and lava above ground.
normal.cn: 在地质学中，这个词与地下的岩浆、地表的熔岩配对使用。

normal.en: Metallurgy supplies the everyday picture: molten iron is poured, never hammered.
normal.cn: 冶金学提供日常图景：铁水只能浇，不能锤。

abstract.en: Picture a candle that has lost its shape but kept all its wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛失去了形状，却保留了全部的蜡。

abstract.en: Picture a winter stream freezing into one flat sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天的小溪冻成一整片平玻璃。

abstract.en: Picture an argument heated until it becomes one glowing thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论被加热到只剩一根发亮的线。

examples.en: The foundry pours molten steel into ingots every four hours.
examples.cn: 铸造厂每隔四小时把钢水浇进钢锭模。

examples.en: Molten rock beneath the ridge pushes the crust upward.
examples.cn: 山脊之下的熔融岩石把地壳向上顶。

examples.en: The glassblower shaped the molten glass with a long iron pipe.
examples.cn: 吹玻璃工用长铁管给熔融玻璃塑形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩（mō）+ 尔（l）+ 腾（tén）」——热到腾起来、化成液体 → 熔化的

root: 古英语 meltan「熔化」的过去分词，属日耳曼语 *meltanan（重构形式）；后缀 -en 标记完成状态。更深来源不确定，与拉丁 mollis「软」的比较仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one physical event: solid material is heated until it can flow, and then that same event is used for glowing light, for casting, for industrial chemistry and finally for emotion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个物理事件展开：固体被加热到可以流动，这个事件随后被用于发光、浇铸、工业化学，最后用于情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a furnace mouth where solid metal leaves its shape and becomes a glowing stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：炉口处，固态金属失去形状，变成一道发光的流体。

branches.en: MATERIALS THAT MELT: iron in a ladle and rock under a volcano obey the same rule.
branches.cn: 会熔的材料：勺里的铁与火山下的岩石遵守同一条规则。

branches.en: FURNACE AND PLANT: glass in a crucible and salt in a thermal tank are both molten media.
branches.cn: 炉与厂：坩埚里的玻璃与热罐里的盐都是熔融介质。

branches.en: GLOW: heat so great that the liquid itself becomes the light source.
branches.cn: 发光：热到液体本身成为光源。

branches.en: CASTING: the liquid is given a shape during the moment it can flow.
branches.cn: 浇铸：在能够流动的那一刻，液体被赋予形状。

branches.en: IMAGE TRANSFER: poured light and molten anger keep the same heat and flow.
branches.cn: 意象转移：倾倒的光与熔岩般的怒火保留了同样的热与流动。

intro.en: Molten is an English participle rather than a Latin compound, but its ending and its family are still readable morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: molten 是英语分词而非拉丁复合词，但它的后缀与词族仍可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin relative is reliable here: the verb is Germanic, and Latin mollis 'soft' is only a hypothesis, so the Latin entries are left empty rather than invented.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有可靠的拉丁同族词：该动词属日耳曼语，拉丁 mollis「软」只是假说，因此拉丁条目留空，不作编造。

items.example: Broken glass lay on the floor.
The molten iron ran along the channel.

items.meaning: in the process of becoming liquid
items.example: The melting ice fed the stream.

items.meaning: water released by melting ice or snow
items.meaningCN: 冰川或积雪融化产生的水

items.meaning: a reactor accident, or a total collapse
items.example: The meltdown ruined the reactor core.
items.exampleCN: 熔毁损毁了反应堆堆芯。

items.example: The coating is meltable at low heat.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂料低温即可熔化。

items.meaning: to melt something a second time
items.example: Scrap steel is remelted in an electric furnace.

definition_zh: 火成的；（岩石）由岩浆冷却凝固形成的；火一般的
definition_en: formed from molten rock that has cooled and solidified; (literary) of, like or produced by fire
core_image: 火山口下的岩浆房慢慢冷却，晶体在暗色玻璃质里一颗颗长出来
scene: 地质队在河谷剖面上敲下一块深色岩石，指着里面的粗大颗粒说明它由地下岩浆缓慢冷却而成。The igneous rock cooled slowly enough for large crystals to grow.
sceneCN: 这里 igneous 指「由岩浆冷却凝固形成的」（第 1 个义项：岩石学三大类中的火成岩）；句意为这块火成岩冷却得足够慢，因而长出了粗大的晶体。可辨识物件：河谷剖面、地质锤、深色岩块、粗大矿物颗粒。

pos.zh: 火成的；岩浆冷却形成的；火一般的

senses.title: Rock formed from cooled magma
senses.titleCN: 由岩浆冷却凝固形成的岩石
senses.definition: of rock: produced when molten material from inside the earth cools and hardens
senses.definitionCN: 指地球内部的熔融物质冷却硬化后形成的岩石
senses.example: The igneous rock cooled slowly enough for large crystals to grow.
senses.exampleCN: 这块火成岩冷却得足够慢，因而长出了粗大的晶体。
senses.why: igneous comes from Latin ignis 'fire', and in the rock classification it names exactly that: rock born from the earth's internal heat, as opposed to rock laid down by water or rebuilt under pressure.
senses.whyCN: igneous 来自拉丁 ignis「火」，在岩石分类中它命名的正是这一点：由地球内部的热生成的岩石，与流水堆积或受压重结晶的岩石相对。

senses.title: Produced by fire or great heat generally
senses.titleCN: 泛指由火或高温生成的
senses.definition: formed or altered by intense heat, not necessarily as a rock
senses.definitionCN: 指由强烈高温生成或改变，不一定是岩石
senses.example: The igneous origin of the deposit is shown by its glassy margins.
senses.exampleCN: 矿体边缘的玻璃质表明它属火成成因。
senses.why: before geology fixed the word, igneous simply meant 'of fire'; that older, wider sense survives in phrases such as igneous origin.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学固定这个词之前，igneous 只是「火的」；这个更早、更宽的义项仍留在 igneous origin（火成成因）这类说法中。

senses.title: Intrusive rock cooled underground
senses.titleCN: 在地下缓慢冷却的侵入岩
senses.definition: of rock that solidified deep below the surface, usually with coarse crystals
senses.definitionCN: 指在地表深处凝固、通常晶体粗大的岩石
senses.example: Granite is an intrusive igneous rock with visible grains.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩是一种颗粒可见的侵入型火成岩。
senses.why: deep cooling is slow cooling, and slow cooling lets crystals grow large; this is why intrusive igneous rock is coarse-grained.
senses.whyCN: 深处冷却就是缓慢冷却，而缓慢冷却让晶体长大；侵入型火成岩因此是粗粒的。

senses.title: Extrusive rock cooled at the surface
senses.titleCN: 在地表快速冷却的喷出岩
senses.definition: of rock that solidified at or near the surface, usually fine-grained or glassy
senses.definitionCN: 指在地表或近地表凝固、通常细粒或玻璃质的岩石
senses.example: Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock that cools within days.
senses.exampleCN: 玄武岩是一种在数日内冷却的喷出型火成岩。
senses.why: The same fire, but cooling at the surface is fast, so crystals have no time to grow; the classification splits one process by cooling speed.
senses.whyCN: 同样是火，但在地表冷却太快，晶体来不及长大；分类正是按冷却速度把这一个过程拆开。

senses.title: An igneous body or intrusion
senses.definition: a mass of igneous rock, such as a sill, dyke or batholith, considered as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 指作为整体看待的火成岩体，如岩床、岩墙或岩基
senses.example: The survey mapped the igneous body along the valley wall.
senses.exampleCN: 测量队沿谷壁标出了这个火成岩体。
senses.why: Once a mass of cooled melt is mapped as a unit, the adjective stops describing the process and starts naming the object.
senses.whyCN: 当一团冷却的熔体被当作单元测绘时，这个形容词就从描述过程转为命名物体。

senses.title: Land built of igneous rock
senses.definition: of a landscape or terrain: made up chiefly of igneous rock
senses.definitionCN: 指主要由火成岩构成的地形或地区
senses.example: The igneous uplands shed water into a hundred streams.
senses.exampleCN: 这片火成岩高地把水送进上百条溪流。
senses.why: Landscapes inherit the rock they are cut from, so a whole upland can be called igneous.
senses.whyCN: 地貌继承它被切割出来的岩石，因此整片高地也可以称为火成的。

senses.title: Fiery, burning, of fire
senses.definition: literary: burning, fiery, or glowing like fire
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：燃烧的、灼热的、像火一样发亮的
senses.example: An igneous sky burned above the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 火一般的天空在沙漠上方燃烧。
senses.why: The word never lost its literal Latin sense, so literature can still use it for burning light.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从未丢掉拉丁语的字面义，因此文学仍可用它描写燃烧的光。

senses.title: Fierce in temper or spirit
senses.definition: figurative: passionate, fierce or explosive in character
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：性情热烈、猛烈或一触即发
senses.example: Her igneous temper matched her red hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她火暴的脾气配得上她那一头红发。
senses.why: Fire as a temperament is a standard metaphor, and the Latin root makes the transfer easy.
senses.whyCN: 把火当作性情是常见比喻，而拉丁词根让这一转移十分自然。

intro.en: Igneous is a Latin adjective built directly on the Latin noun for fire, and it entered English as a learned word before geology made it a technical term.
intro.cn: igneous 是直接由拉丁语「火」这一名词构成的形容词，作为学术词进入英语，后来才被地质学用作术语。

items.en: Ignis is the Latin noun for 'fire', a third-declension noun with the stem ign-. It is one of the oldest words in the language and appears in compounds such as ignifer 'fire-bearing'.
items.cn: ignis 是拉丁语「火」的名词，属第三变格法，词干为 ign-；它是语言中最古老的词之一，出现在 ignifer「带火的」这类复合词中。

items.en: The adjective igneus 'of fire, fiery, burning' was formed with the suffix -eus 'of the nature of', giving the exact shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 形容词 igneus「火的、燃烧的」由后缀 -eus「具……性质的」构成，正是英语借入的形状。

items.en: *H₁n̥gʷnis is a reconstruction supported by Sanskrit agni and Lithuanian ugnis 'fire'; Latin ignis belongs to the same family, though the exact Latin development involves sound changes that are reconstructed.
items.cn: *h₁n̥gʷnis 是重构形式，依据梵语 agni 与立陶宛语 ugnis「火」；拉丁 ignis 属同一词族，但拉丁语的具体音变过程属重构。

items.en: The adjective appears in English scientific writing in the seventeenth century in the general sense 'produced by fire', alongside older Latin-based vocabulary.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪英语科学文献中出现，通义为「由火生成的」，与更早的拉丁语借词同时使用。

items.en: In the late eighteenth century the new science of geology adopted igneous for rock solidified from magma, and the word became one of the three great rock classes.
items.cn: 十八世纪晚期，新兴的地质学采用 igneous 指由岩浆凝固的岩石，这个词遂成为三大岩类之一。

items.en: Source uncertain (only deeper reconstruction): the Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested, so any statement about the earliest form of the word is a reconstruction, not a record.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深层属重构）：印欧词根是重构而非实证，因此关于该词最早形式的任何说法都属重构，而非记录。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that resemble igneous in spelling but come from other roots; group two holds words for rock and heat that are often used beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写近似但词根不同的形容词；第二组是常与它并用的岩石与高温词。

entries.definition: Means clever and inventive, from Latin ingenium 'inborn talent' (in- 'in' plus gignere 'beget'); no fire is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 意为机巧、有发明天才，来自拉丁 ingenium「天生的才能」（in-「内」加 gignere「生育」）；与火无关。

entries.definition: Means woody or wood-like, from Latin lignum 'wood' plus the same -eus ending; it shares the suffix, not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 意为木质的、像木头的，来自拉丁 lignum「木」加同一个 -eus 后缀；共享后缀，不共享词根。

entries.definition: Means base or dishonourable, from Latin in- 'not' plus gnobilis 'known, noble'; the ign- here is a negative prefix, not 'fire'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为卑劣的、不光彩的，来自拉丁 in-「不」加 gnobilis「知名的、高贵的」；这里的 ign- 是否定前缀，不是「火」。

entries.definition: To set on fire, from Latin ignitus, the past participle of ignire 'to set fire to'; it is a true relative, not a look-alike, and the tag marks it as such.
entries.definitionCN: 指点燃，来自拉丁 ignitus，即 ignire「放火」的过去分词；它是真正的同族词而非形近词，标签已标明。

entries.definition: Describes things produced by a volcano or its erupted material; igneous is the wider rock-class word, volcanic stresses the surface vent.
entries.definitionCN: 指火山或其喷出物形成的；igneous 是更宽的岩类词，volcanic 强调地表喷口。

entries.definition: Relates specifically to magma, the molten material below the surface; igneous covers both magma and lava products.
entries.definitionCN: 专指地表之下的熔融物质岩浆；igneous 同时涵盖岩浆与熔岩产物。

entries.definition: A geological term for igneous rock that solidified deep underground, named after Pluto, god of the underworld.
entries.definitionCN: 地质术语，指在地下深处凝固的火成岩，得名于冥界之神普路托。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for something burning or very hot; igneous carries the same idea only in literary or technical use.
entries.definitionCN: 指燃烧或极热的日常形容词；igneous 只在文学或技术用法中承载同样的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real suffix and the real rock-class vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的后缀与真实的岩类词汇。

normal.en: Ign- is Latin ignis 'fire', the same root as in ignite and ignition.
normal.cn: ign- 是拉丁 ignis「火」，与 ignite、ignition 同根。

normal.en: -eous means 'of the nature of', as in ligneous and aqueous, so igneous is literally 'of the nature of fire'.
normal.cn: -eous 意为「具……性质的」，如 ligneous、aqueous，因此 igneous 字面就是「具火性的」。

normal.en: The rock triad is igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic.
normal.cn: 三大岩类是火成岩、沉积岩、变质岩。

normal.en: Intrusive igneous rock cools slowly and is coarse; extrusive cools fast and is fine.
normal.cn: 侵入型火成岩冷却慢、颗粒粗；喷出型冷却快、颗粒细。

normal.en: Latin ignis also gives ignis fatuus, the will-o'-the-wisp.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ignis 还衍生 ignis fatuus，即鬼火。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed room of magma slowly growing its own glassy furniture.
abstract.cn: 想象一间封闭的岩浆房，慢慢长出玻璃质的家具。

abstract.en: Picture a fire that leaves behind a stone copy of itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一场火留下了一块自己的石头复制品。

abstract.en: Picture heat as a sculptor working only with cooling.
abstract.cn: 想象高温是一位只会用冷却来雕刻的雕塑家。

examples.en: Geologists divide rocks into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic classes.
examples.cn: 地质学家把岩石分为火成岩、沉积岩与变质岩三类。

examples.en: The igneous intrusion cut across older sedimentary layers.
examples.cn: 这块火成侵入体切穿了更古老的沉积层。

examples.en: An igneous dye of orange spread across the evening sky.
examples.cn: 火一般的橙色染遍了傍晚的天空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个（ig）你（ne）俄斯（ous）」——从火里生出来的石头 → 火成的

root: 拉丁 ignis「火」+ -eus「具……性质的」→ igneus「火的」；ignis 与梵语 agni、立陶宛语 ugnis 同族，印欧词根 *h₁n̥gʷnis 属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one birth: molten material cools into stone, and that single event then supplies the rock class, its deep and shallow varieties, the landscape made of it, and finally the literary image of fire in a temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次诞生展开：熔融物质冷却成石，这一事件随后提供岩类、它的深成与浅成变体、由它构成的地貌，最后是性情中火的文学意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cooling magma chamber in which crystals grow out of a dark liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷却中的岩浆房，晶体从暗色液体里长出来。

branches.en: BORN OF HEAT: whether the product is a rock or an ore body, fire is its cause.
branches.cn: 生于热：无论产物是岩石还是矿体，火都是其成因。

branches.en: TWO SPEEDS: slow cooling underground makes coarse grains, fast cooling at the surface makes fine ones.
branches.cn: 两种速度：地下慢冷产生粗粒，地表快冷产生细粒。

branches.en: A BODY AND A LAND: an intrusion can be mapped as one mass, and a whole upland can be built of such masses.
branches.cn: 一个岩体与一片土地：侵入体可作为整体测绘，整片高地也可由这类岩体构成。

branches.en: FIRE IN THE SKY: the adjective returns to its literal root and describes burning light.
branches.cn: 天上之火：该形容词回到字面词根，描写燃烧的光。

branches.en: FIRE IN A PERSON: the same heat becomes a temperament.
branches.cn: 人之火：同样的热变成一种性情。

intro.en: Igneous is a Latin adjective whose root and suffix both recur in English, so the word can be read as two morphemes plus a geological setting.
intro.cn: igneous 是拉丁形容词，词根与后缀都在英语中反复出现，因此可按两个语素加一个地质语境来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin ignis 'fire' yields igneous, ignite, ignition and the phrase ignis fatuus; the suffix -eus 'of the nature of' also appears in ligneous and aqueous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ignis「火」衍生 igneous、ignite、ignition 与 ignis fatuus 这一短语；后缀 -eus「具……性质的」也出现在 ligneous 与 aqueous 中。

items.structure: ignis (Latin noun, third declension, stem ign-)
items.example: Ignis supplied the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: ignis 提供了整个词族的词根。

items.example: Aqueous means 'of the nature of water'.

items.meaning: of fire; formed by cooling melt
items.meaningCN: 火的；由熔体冷却形成的

items.meaning: the act or device of setting fire
able to be set on fire
a rock formed from a glowing ash flow
items.meaningCN: 由炽热火山灰流形成的熔结凝灰岩
items.example: The ignimbrite welded into a hard sheet.
items.exampleCN: 熔结凝灰岩焊结成坚硬的板状。

items.example: The plan proved an ignis fatuus.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划终成一场空想。

latinEntries.structure: igneus, ignea, igneum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 沉积物；沉淀物；泥沙；沉淀（动词）
definition_en: solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid, or that is carried and laid down by water, wind or ice
core_image: 浑浊的河水在入海口慢下来，细沙一粒粒沉到瓶底，清水留在上层
scene: 河水灌进玻璃瓶，静置到第二天早晨，细泥沉到瓶底，上层的液体变清了。Fine sediment settled to the bottom of the jar by morning.
sceneCN: 这里 sediment 指「液体中沉降到底部的固体颗粒」（第 1 个义项：沉积下来的泥沙等固体物质）；句意为细小的沉积物在夜里沉到瓶底。可辨识物件：玻璃瓶、浑浊河水、瓶底细泥、上层清水。

senses.title: Material laid down by water, wind or ice
senses.titleCN: 由水、风或冰堆积下来的物质
senses.definition: solid particles carried by water, wind or ice and left behind when the carrier loses energy
senses.definitionCN: 指被水、风或冰搬运、在搬运介质失去能量后留下的固体颗粒
senses.example: Fine sediment settled to the bottom of the jar by morning.
senses.exampleCN: 细小的沉积物在夜里沉到了瓶底。
senses.why: Sedere 'to sit' plus -mentum 'result' gives 'what has sat down'; the word names the material only after it has stopped moving.
senses.whyCN: sedere「坐」加 -mentum「结果」给出「已经坐下来的东西」；这个词只在那物质停止移动之后才命名它。

senses.title: Solids that settle in a liquid
senses.titleCN: 液体中沉到底部的固体
senses.definition: the solid matter that sinks to the bottom of a standing liquid
senses.definitionCN: 指在静置液体中下沉到底部的固体物质
senses.example: A dark sediment gathered at the bottom of the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶底部积起一层深色沉淀。
senses.why: It is the same settling seen in a kitchen: any liquid left standing leaves its solids behind.
senses.whyCN: 这是厨房里也能见到的同一种沉降：任何静置的液体都会把固体留在底部。

senses.title: A deposited layer or stratum
senses.titleCN: 沉积形成的一层或一层岩层
senses.definition: a single bed or layer of deposited material, often visible as a band
senses.definitionCN: 指沉积形成的一层材料，常呈带状可见
senses.example: Each sediment band records a different flood.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层沉积都记录了一次不同的洪水。
senses.why: Once the deposit is thick enough to see, it becomes a layer, and the noun moves from material to a visible band.
senses.whyCN: 一旦沉积厚到肉眼可见，它就成了一层，名词也从材料转向可见的层带。

senses.title: Suspended load in moving water
senses.definition: particles held in suspension in a river or current, measured as water quality
senses.definitionCN: 指河流或水流中悬而未落的颗粒，作为水质指标测定
senses.example: The dam traps sediment that once reached the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝拦住了原本到达三角洲的悬移质。
senses.why: Particles that have not yet settled are still sediment, so the word follows the material through its whole journey.
senses.whyCN: 尚未落下的颗粒仍然是 sediment，因此这个词跟着物质走完整个搬运过程。

senses.title: Lees at the bottom of wine or vinegar
senses.definition: the deposit of dead yeast and particles found in wine, cider or vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 指葡萄酒、苹果酒或醋中死酵母与颗粒形成的沉渣
senses.example: Pour the wine slowly so the sediment stays in the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢倒酒，让沉渣留在瓶里。
senses.why: Wine lees are the household version of the geological process, so the same noun serves both.
senses.whyCN: 酒渣是这一地质过程在厨房里的版本，因此同一个名词两边都用。

senses.title: Accumulated remains of the past
senses.titleCN: 比喻：历史或记忆的层层积存
senses.definition: figurative: the accumulated, slowly deposited remains of an earlier period
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：较早时期缓慢积存下来的遗留物
senses.example: Old letters lay in the sediment of family memory.
senses.exampleCN: 旧信件沉在家族记忆的底层。
senses.why: The metaphor works because memory also deposits slowly and in layers, with older things lower down.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为记忆也缓慢、分层地沉积，越老的东西越靠下。

senses.title: To deposit as sediment (technical verb)
senses.definition: to cause particles to settle out of a liquid, or to deposit them
senses.definitionCN: 指使颗粒从液体中沉降出来，或把它们沉积下来
senses.example: The current sediments sand along the inner bend.
senses.exampleCN: 水流把砂沉积在内侧河弯。
senses.why: English verbs form freely from nouns, and technical writing needs a verb for the act of depositing.
senses.whyCN: 英语动词可由名词自由构成，而技术写作需要一个动词来表达「使沉积」这一动作。

senses.title: The geological archive of a basin
senses.definition: the whole body of deposits in a basin, read as a record of past environments
senses.definitionCN: 指盆地中全部沉积体，被当作过去环境的记录来解读
senses.example: The sediment of the lake bed spans ten thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 湖底的沉积层跨越了一万年。
senses.why: A basin's whole fill is read as a record, so the mass noun becomes a collective archive.
senses.whyCN: 盆地的全部充填物被当作记录来读，于是这个物质名词变成了集体档案。

intro.en: Sediment comes from the Latin noun for a settling, built on the verb 'to sit'. The geological sense is a later specialization of a very general image.
intro.cn: sediment 来自拉丁语表示「沉降」的名词，由动词「坐、停留」构成；地质义是这个极普遍意象后来的专门化。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit, stay, settle' is a second-conjugation verb with the stem sed-, and it underlies a large family: session, resident, sedentary, sedative.
items.cn: sedere「坐、停留、安定」是第二变格法动词，词干 sed-，支撑起一个大家族：session、resident、sedentary、sedative。

items.en: Sedimentum 'a settling, a sinking down, dregs' was formed with -mentum, the suffix for the result of an action, so the noun names what has settled rather than the settling itself.
items.cn: sedimentum「沉降、沉下、渣滓」由 -mentum 构成，这个后缀表示动作的结果，因此名词命名的是「沉下来的东西」，而不是「下沉」这一动作。

items.en: English took the word through French sédiment in the sixteenth century, first for dregs and earthy matter in liquids.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪经法语 sédiment 借入这个词，最初指液体中的渣滓与土质物。

items.en: From the eighteenth century sediment was applied to sand, mud and gravel laid down by water, and the noun became central to stratigraphy.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，sediment 被用于水所堆积的砂、泥与砾石，这个名词成为地层学的核心。

items.en: The verb sedimented appears later, chiefly in technical writing, where it means to settle out or to deposit particles.
items.cn: 动词 sedimented 出现较晚，主要用于技术写作，意为沉降析出或使颗粒沉积。

items.en: Not uncertain: the derivation from sedere is established. What is reconstructed is the Indo-European root *sed- 'sit', which is inferred from Sanskrit and Greek cognates rather than attested directly.
items.cn: 并非存疑：源自 sedere 这一点是确定的。属重构的是印欧词根 *sed-「坐」，它由梵语与希腊语同族词推断而来，而非直接实证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like sediment but come from other roots; group two holds materials and processes often named beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的词；第二组是常与它并称的材料与过程词。

entries.definition: Means a feeling or opinion, from Latin sentire 'to feel'; the shared letters sed- are accidental, since the root here is sent-.
entries.definitionCN: 意为情感或看法，来自拉丁 sentire「感觉」；共同的字母只是巧合，这里的词根是 sent-。

entries.definition: A calming drug, from sedare 'to settle, calm', a causative form of sedere; it shares the root 'sit' but means 'making something settle down'.
entries.definitionCN: 指镇静药，来自 sedare「使安定」，是 sedere 的使动形式；它共享「坐」的词根，但意思是「使某物安定下来」。

entries.definition: Means sitting much or fixed in one place, from sedere plus -ary; it is a true relative and describes the posture, not the deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为久坐的、固定一处的，来自 sedere 加 -ary；它是真正的同族词，描写姿势而非沉积物。

entries.definition: A meeting or sitting of a body, from sedere through Latin sessio; related in root, unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指机构的一次会议或开庭，经拉丁 sessio 来自 sedere；词根相关，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any material left by a natural process, or the act of laying it down; it is the wider word that sediment belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何自然过程留下的物质或堆积动作；它是 sediment 所属的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Specifically sediment of grains between sand and clay in size; it is one size class of sediment, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 特指粒径介于砂与黏土之间的细粒沉积物；它只是沉积物的一个粒级，不是同义词。

entries.definition: Thick wet waste from sewage or industry; it stresses pollution and disposal, while sediment is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指污水或工业产生的黏稠湿废物；它强调污染与处置，sediment 则是中性词。

entries.definition: Solid matter thrown out of a solution by a chemical reaction, not by simple settling; chemistry keeps the two apart.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学反应从溶液中析出的固体，而非单纯沉降；化学上二者区分明确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real suffix and the real geological phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀与真实的地质搭配。

normal.en: Sedere 'to sit' plus -mentum 'result': the stuff that has sat down at the bottom.
normal.cn: sedere「坐」加 -mentum「结果」：已经坐到底部的东西。

normal.en: The family runs sediment, sedimentary, sedimentation, sedimentology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sediment、sedimentary、sedimentation、sedimentology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fine sediment, suspended sediment, sediment core, sediment transport.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细沉积物、悬浮沉积物、沉积柱样、沉积物搬运。

normal.en: The same root gives session, resident and sedentary, all about sitting or staying.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 session、resident、sedentary，都与坐或停留有关。

normal.en: In a river the sediment travels high in flood and rests low in drought.
normal.cn: 在河里，沉积物洪水时高悬、枯水时落底。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that records time by dropping sand instead of moving hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一座靠落沙而非指针记录时间的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every reader leaves one grain on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每位读者都在地板上留下一粒沙。

abstract.en: Picture a river writing its diary in mud at the bottom of a lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河在湖底用泥写下自己的日记。

examples.en: The reservoir is filling with sediment faster than expected.
examples.cn: 水库正以超出预期的速度被泥沙填满。

examples.en: A core of lake sediment shows layers of ash from old eruptions.
examples.cn: 一根湖底沉积柱样显示出古老喷发留下的层层火山灰。

examples.en: Let the vinegar stand until the sediment sinks.
examples.cn: 让醋静置到沉渣落下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞（se）底（di）闷（ment）」——塞在底下的东西 → 沉积物、沉淀

root: 拉丁 sedere「坐、停留」+ -mentum（动作结果）→ sedimentum「沉降、沉渣」；英语经法语 sédiment 借入。印欧词根 *sed-「坐」属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one motion: particles lose their energy and sit down, and that single settling then becomes a layer, a load, a wine lees, a family memory, a verb and finally a whole archive.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：颗粒失去能量而落下，这一次沉降随后变成一层、一份载荷、一份酒渣、一段家族记忆、一个动词，最后成为一整部档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grains falling through still water and coming to rest on the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：颗粒穿过静水落下，停在底部。

branches.en: SETTLING: the physical act is the same in a river, a kettle and a jar.
branches.cn: 沉降：河、壶、瓶中的物理动作相同。

branches.en: LAYER UPON LAYER: one band is an event, and the whole stack is an archive.
branches.cn: 层层相叠：一层是一次事件，整叠则是一部档案。

branches.en: ON THE MOVE: before it settles, the same material is a suspended load and a water-quality problem.
branches.cn: 搬运之中：在沉降之前，同样的物质是悬移质，也是水质问题。

branches.en: IN A BOTTLE: wine lees are the same settling seen in a kitchen.
branches.cn: 瓶中：酒渣是同一沉降在厨房里的样子。

branches.en: FROM NOUN TO VERB AND TO MEMORY: what settles can be laid down deliberately, or remembered slowly.
branches.cn: 从名词到动词与记忆：沉下的东西可以被有意堆积，也可以被缓慢记住。

intro.en: Sediment is built from a Latin verb plus a result suffix, and both pieces recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: sediment 由拉丁动词加结果后缀构成，这两部分在英语的大家族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere 'to sit' gives sediment, session, resident, sedentary and sedative; -mentum marks the result of an action, as in monumentum and argumentum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sedere「坐」衍生 sediment、session、resident、sedentary 与 sedative；-mentum 标记动作结果，如 monumentum 与 argumentum。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根描写归于静止。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of settling into the thing settled.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「沉降」这一动作变成沉下来的东西。

items.example: Fine sediment settled in the jar.
The cliff is made of sedimentary rock.

沉积作用填满了旧河道。
沉积学解释了这些波痕。

items.example: A sedimentological study followed the core.

沉积学家测定了各层的年代。

items.example: The council held a long session.
items.exampleCN: 议会开了长时间的一次会议。

definition_zh: 沉积的；沉积岩的；由沉积物形成的
definition_en: relating to sediment, or made of material deposited in layers by water, wind or ice
core_image: 河谷崖壁上层层平行的岩板，像被压平的沙层一页页叠着
scene: 野外课上，学生用锤子敲开一层层平整的岩石，看到沙粒被压成了薄薄的板。The cliff is built of sedimentary layers laid down under an ancient sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sedimentary 指「由沉积物逐层堆积形成的」（第 1 个义项：沉积成因的，尤指沉积岩）；句意为这处崖壁由古老海底逐层堆积的沉积岩构成。可辨识物件：崖壁、平行层理、地质锤、砂质岩板。

pos.zh: 沉积的；沉积成的；沉积岩的

senses.title: Relating to sediment
senses.definition: of or concerning sediment as a material
senses.definitionCN: 指与作为物质的沉积物有关的
senses.example: The sedimentary particles range from clay to coarse sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这些沉积颗粒从黏土一直到粗砂。
senses.why: The suffix -ary means 'connected with', so the adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ary 意为「与……相关的」，因此这个形容词只是把名词连接到它所描述的对象。

senses.title: Formed by layer-by-layer deposition
senses.definition: formed by the accumulation and consolidation of deposited material
senses.definitionCN: 指由沉积物累积并固结而成
senses.example: The cliff is built of sedimentary layers laid down under an ancient sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这处崖壁由古老海底逐层堆积的沉积岩构成。
senses.why: 'Formed by layers' is the defining trait that separates this rock class from cooled melt and from pressed schist.
senses.whyCN: 「逐层形成」是这一岩类区别于冷却熔体与受压片岩的关键特征。

senses.title: Of the rock class so formed
senses.titleCN: 属于沉积岩这一岩类的
senses.definition: of rock: belonging to the class produced by deposition, as opposed to igneous or metamorphic
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石属于沉积成因的一类，与火成岩、变质岩相对
senses.example: Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 砂岩与石灰岩是沉积岩。
senses.why: Classification needs one word for the whole family, and this adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要用一个词指称整个岩族，这个形容词正好承担这一职能。

senses.title: Filling a depositional basin
senses.definition: of a basin: filled with deposited material over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 指盆地长期充填沉积物质
senses.example: The sedimentary basin holds kilometres of fill.
senses.exampleCN: 这个沉积盆地充填了数千米厚的物质。
senses.why: A basin is defined by what fills it, so the adjective marks the container by its contents.
senses.whyCN: 盆地由充填它的东西来定义，因此这个形容词用内容物来标记容器。

senses.title: Showing bedding or stratification
senses.definition: of a structure: showing the layering produced by deposition
senses.definitionCN: 指构造显示出沉积造成的成层性
senses.example: Cross-bedding is a sedimentary structure.
senses.exampleCN: 交错层理是一种沉积构造。
senses.why: Visible bedding is the physical proof of deposition, hence the fixed phrase sedimentary structure.
senses.whyCN: 可见层理是沉积的物理证据，因此有 sedimentary structure（沉积构造）这一固定说法。

senses.title: Belonging to a depositional cycle
senses.definition: of a cycle: beginning with deposition and ending with exposure or uplift
senses.definitionCN: 指以沉积开始、以暴露或抬升结束的旋回
senses.example: Each sedimentary cycle ends with a gap in the record.
senses.exampleCN: 每个沉积旋回都以记录中的一次间断结束。
senses.why: A cycle is deposition followed by exposure, and the adjective marks the depositional half.
senses.whyCN: 一个旋回是先沉积后暴露，这个形容词标记的是沉积的那一半。

senses.title: Formed by chemical or biological deposition
senses.titleCN: 由化学或生物作用沉积形成的
senses.definition: of deposits: produced by precipitation or by living organisms rather than clastic settling
senses.definitionCN: 指由沉淀作用或生物作用形成，而非碎屑沉降
senses.example: The sedimentary iron ore formed by precipitation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座沉积铁矿由沉淀作用形成。
senses.why: Not all sediment is broken fragments; chemical and biological precipitation also deposit, and the adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有沉积物都是碎屑；化学与生物沉淀同样在沉积，这个形容词两者都涵盖。

senses.title: Of the geological record these rocks keep
senses.titleCN: 指这些岩石保存的地质记录
senses.definition: of the record: the history preserved in deposited sequences
senses.definitionCN: 指保存在沉积序列中的历史
senses.example: The sedimentary record shows three marine invasions.
senses.exampleCN: 沉积记录显示出三次海侵。
senses.why: The record is the sum of all the layers, so the adjective extends from single beds to the whole archive.
senses.whyCN: 记录是全部岩层的总和，因此这个形容词从单层扩展到整部档案。

intro.en: Sedimentary is an English adjective formed on the noun sediment, which itself goes back to Latin sedere 'to sit'.
intro.cn: sedimentary 是在名词 sediment 上构成的英语形容词，而 sediment 本身可上溯到拉丁 sedere「坐」。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit, settle' supplies the root of the whole family, and its past participle sessum underlies words such as session.
items.cn: sedere「坐、安定」提供整个词族的词根，其过去分词 sessum 支撑 session 这类词。

items.en: Sedimentum named the result of settling, and English borrowed it through French as sediment in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: sedimentum 命名沉降的结果，英语在十六世纪经法语把它借入为 sediment。

items.en: The Latin adjectival suffix -arius, through French -aire and English -ary, means 'connected with', giving sedimentary 'connected with sediment'.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀 -arius 经法语 -aire 与英语 -ary，意为「与……相关的」，由此得到 sedimentary「与沉积物相关的」。

items.en: The adjective became a standard rock-class term in nineteenth-century geology, pairing with igneous and metamorphic.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪地质学中成为标准的岩类术语，与 igneous（火成的）、metamorphic（变质的）并列。

items.en: Later phrases such as sedimentary basin, sedimentary structure and sedimentary cycle extended the adjective across the whole discipline.
items.cn: 后来 sedimentary basin（沉积盆地）、sedimentary structure（沉积构造）与 sedimentary cycle（沉积旋回）等说法把这个形容词扩展到整个学科。

items.en: Not uncertain: the derivation is established. Only the precise date of the first geological use is uncertain, and the older Indo-European root *sed- is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 并非存疑：派生关系是确定的。仅首次用于地质学义的准确年代不确定，更早的印欧词根 *sed- 属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes with other roots; group two holds adjectives describing how rock is made.
note.cn: 第一组是词根不同的形近词；第二组是描写岩石成因的形容词。

entries.definition: Means given to sitting, from sedere plus -ary; it shares root and suffix with sedimentary but describes a way of life, not a rock.
entries.definitionCN: 意为久坐的，来自 sedere 加 -ary；它与 sedimentary 共享词根与后缀，却描写生活方式而非岩石。

entries.definition: Means basic or introductory, from elementum 'first principle'; the ending is the same, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 意为基本的、初级的，来自 elementum「基本要素」；词尾相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Means governed by tender feeling, from sentire 'to feel'; it looks close but has no connection with settling.
entries.definitionCN: 意为受柔情支配的，来自 sentire「感觉」；外形接近，但与沉降无关。

entries.definition: Means lasting only a moment, from moment plus -ary; it shares the long ending but comes from a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为只持续一瞬的，由 moment 加 -ary 构成；共享长词尾，但名词词根不同。

entries.definition: Means relating to deposition as an action; sedimentary describes the material or rock that results.
entries.definitionCN: 指与沉积这一动作相关的；sedimentary 描写由此产生的材料或岩石。

entries.definition: Means arranged in layers, from stratum 'spread-out thing'; it names the visible layering that sedimentary rock usually shows.
entries.definitionCN: 意为成层的，来自 stratum「铺开之物」；它命名沉积岩通常显示的可见层理。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for rock made of broken pieces, from Greek klastos 'broken'; it is one kind of sedimentary rock, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指由碎屑构成的岩石，来自希腊 klastos「破碎的」；它只是沉积岩的一类，不是同义词。

entries.definition: Means deposited by flowing water, from Latin alluvio 'a washing against'; it narrows sedimentary to river action.
entries.definitionCN: 指由流水沉积的，来自拉丁 alluvio「冲积」；它把 sedimentary 收窄到河流作用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real root, the real suffix and the real rock-class triple.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词根、真实的后缀与真实的三大岩类。

normal.en: Sediment plus -ary: 'connected with sediment', exactly as the suffix says.
normal.cn: sediment 加 -ary：正如后缀所示，「与沉积物相关的」。

normal.en: The rock triple is igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic.
normal.cn: 三大岩类是火成岩、沉积岩、变质岩。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sedimentary rock, sedimentary layer, sedimentary basin, sedimentary structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：沉积岩、沉积层、沉积盆地、沉积构造。

normal.en: The family climbs sediment, sedimentary, sedimentation, sedimentology.
normal.cn: 词族按 sediment、sedimentary、sedimentation、sedimentology 逐级展开。

normal.en: Layering is the giveaway: sedimentary rock comes in sheets, not in one cooled mass.
normal.cn: 成层是它的标志：沉积岩成片状，而不是一整块冷却的熔体。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of newspapers pressed into one hard board.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠报纸被压成一块硬板。

abstract.en: Picture a beach writing its own autobiography grain by grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海滩一粒一粒地写自传。

abstract.en: Picture time stored as thickness instead of as numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象时间以厚度而不是数字来储存。

examples.en: The sedimentary sequence records a shallow sea that lasted a million years.
examples.cn: 这套沉积序列记录了一片存在百万年的浅海。

examples.en: Sedimentary basins along the margin trap oil and gas.
examples.cn: 边缘的沉积盆地圈闭了石油与天然气。

examples.en: A sedimentary deposit of gypsum formed as the lake dried.
examples.cn: 湖泊干涸时形成了石膏沉积矿床。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞底（sedi）门（ment）特瑞（ary）」——塞在底下一层层压成的 → 沉积的

root: 拉丁 sedere「坐、安定」+ -mentum（结果）→ sedimentum，再加 -arius「与……相关的」→ sedimentary；词根与沉积作用同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective around one process: material settles, hardens, shows layers, fills basins and finally becomes a readable record of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个形容词围绕同一个过程展开：物质沉降、固结、显出层理、充填盆地，最后成为可解读的时间记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat sheets of hardened sand stacked like pages in a book.
core.cn: 核心意象：压硬的砂层像书页一样平叠着。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND PROCESS: the adjective first names the stuff and then the way it was laid down.
branches.cn: 材料与过程：这个形容词先命名物质，再命名堆积方式。

branches.en: THE ROCK CLASS: one of the three great families, defined by deposition rather than by heat or pressure.
branches.cn: 岩类：三大岩族之一，以沉积而非热或压力来定义。

branches.en: SPACE AND TIME: a basin fills through cycles, each closing with a gap.
branches.cn: 空间与时间：盆地经由旋回充填，每个旋回以一次间断收尾。

branches.en: STRUCTURES AND CHEMISTRY: bedding shows the process, and precipitation adds a non-clastic route.
branches.cn: 构造与化学：层理显示过程，沉淀作用补充了非碎屑的途径。

branches.en: THE RECORD: what was deposited becomes the archive that geologists read.
branches.cn: 记录：沉积下来的东西成为地质学家解读的档案。

intro.en: Sedimentary combines the noun sediment with the Latin-derived suffix -ary, and the whole family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: sedimentary 把名词 sediment 与拉丁来源的后缀 -ary 组合起来，整个词族都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere 'to sit' and -mentum 'result' give sediment; -arius 'connected with' gives the adjective, as in elementary and military.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sedere「坐」与 -mentum「结果」构成 sediment；-arius「与……相关的」构成该形容词，如 elementary 与 military。

items.example: The root carries the idea of coming to rest.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带有归于静止的意思。
沉积物就是已经沉下来的东西。
military 意为与士兵相关的。
这处崖壁是沉积成因的。
沉积学家在河床上取样。

definition_zh: 沉积作用；沉淀；沉降（过程）
definition_en: the process by which particles settle out of a liquid or are deposited as layers of sediment
core_image: 量筒里浑浊的泥水静置，颗粒按粗细一层层落到筒底，上层渐渐澄清
scene: 实验台上，浑浊的泥水在量筒里静置，颗粒按大小一层层落到筒底。Sedimentation in the cylinder separated the mud into bands of different grain size.
sceneCN: 这里 sedimentation 指「颗粒从液体中沉降、逐层堆积的过程」（第 1 个义项：沉积作用，既包括水中沉降也包括地质堆积）；句意为量筒中的沉降把泥分成不同粒级的层带。可辨识物件：量筒、浑浊泥水、分层沉积物、澄清的上清液。

pos.zh: 沉积作用；沉淀；沉降过程

senses.title: Deposition of particles in a liquid
senses.definition: the process by which suspended particles sink and come to rest at the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 指悬浮颗粒下沉并停在底部的过程
senses.example: Sedimentation in the cylinder separated the mud into bands of different grain size.
senses.exampleCN: 量筒中的沉降把泥分成不同粒级的层带。
senses.why: 'The process' is exactly what -ation adds to the noun.
senses.whyCN: 「过程」正是 -ation 加在名词上所带来的意思。

senses.title: Geological accumulation of sediment
senses.definition: the natural laying down of sediment by water, wind or ice over long periods
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风或冰在长时间内自然堆积沉积物
senses.example: Rapid sedimentation filled the lake within a century.
senses.exampleCN: 快速沉积在一个世纪内填满了这个湖。
senses.why: Geological deposition is the same settling at a larger scale and over a longer time.
senses.whyCN: 地质堆积是同一种沉降在更大尺度、更长时间上的表现。

senses.title: Formation of layered strata
senses.definition: the building of successive beds that later harden into sedimentary rock
senses.definitionCN: 指逐层堆积、后来硬化成沉积岩的过程
senses.example: Sedimentation built the sandstone benches along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 沉积作用造就了河边的砂岩阶地。
senses.why: Layers are the visible result, so the process noun also covers their building.
senses.whyCN: 岩层是可见的结果，因此这个动作名词也涵盖它们的建造。

senses.title: Settling in water and waste treatment
senses.titleCN: 水处理与废水处理中的沉淀
senses.definition: the settling stage in a treatment plant, where solids are removed from water
senses.definitionCN: 指处理厂中把固体从水中除去的沉降环节
senses.example: Primary sedimentation removes most of the suspended solids.
senses.exampleCN: 初次沉淀去除了大部分悬浮固体。
senses.why: Treatment plants borrow the natural process and speed it up in tanks.
senses.whyCN: 处理厂借用这一自然过程，并在池中把它加快。

senses.title: Separation in the laboratory
senses.definition: the use of settling or centrifuging to separate particles by size or density
senses.definitionCN: 指利用沉降或离心按粒径或密度分离颗粒
senses.example: Sedimentation analysis gives the grain-size distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 沉降分析给出粒度分布。
senses.why: Laboratory separation uses the same physics under controlled conditions.
senses.whyCN: 实验室分离在受控条件下使用同一套物理规律。

senses.title: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate
senses.definition: a medical test measuring how fast red cells settle in a tube, used as a sign of inflammation
senses.definitionCN: 指测量红细胞在管中沉降速度的医学检验，用作炎症指标
senses.example: A raised sedimentation rate suggested an infection.
senses.exampleCN: 血沉升高提示可能存在感染。
senses.why: Medicine measures the settling of red cells and names the test after the process.
senses.whyCN: 医学测量红细胞的沉降，并以这一过程来命名该检验。

senses.title: Settling of precipitates in industry
senses.definition: the settling of chemically formed solids in tanks before filtration
senses.definitionCN: 指化学生成的固体在过滤前于池中沉降
senses.example: Sedimentation thickened the slurry before filtration.
senses.exampleCN: 沉降在过滤前使泥浆增稠。
senses.why: Industry settles chemical precipitates before filtration, another application of the same word.
senses.whyCN: 工业在过滤前让化学沉淀物沉降，这是同一个词的又一应用。

senses.title: Accumulation as a measurable rate
senses.definition: the rate at which material is deposited, expressed per unit time
senses.definitionCN: 指物质堆积的速率，以单位时间表示
senses.example: The sedimentation rate rose after the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝建成后沉积速率上升。
senses.why: Once timing is added, the process becomes a rate, and the noun carries that measurement.
senses.whyCN: 一旦加入时间，过程就变成速率，这个名词也承载这一测量。

intro.en: Sedimentation is the noun of action built on sediment, which descends from Latin sedere 'to sit'.
intro.cn: sedimentation 是在 sediment 上构成的动作名词，而 sediment 源自拉丁 sedere「坐」。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit, settle' is the base verb, with the stem sed- and a large family in English.
items.cn: sedere「坐、安定」是基础动词，词干 sed-，在英语中有庞大的词族。

items.en: Sedimentum 'a settling, dregs' was formed with the result suffix -mentum and passed through French into English.
items.cn: sedimentum「沉降、沉渣」由结果后缀 -mentum 构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The Latin suffix -atio, -ationis names an action or its result, so sedimentation is the act of settling rather than the settled material.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -atio、-ationis 命名动作或其结果，因此 sedimentation 指沉降这一动作，而非沉下来的物质。

items.en: The noun spread with industrial water treatment and with geology in the nineteenth century, where it named both natural deposition and engineered settling.
items.cn: 这个名词在十九世纪随工业水处理与地质学传播，同时指自然沉积与工程沉降。

items.en: In the twentieth century sedimentation rate became a standard clinical phrase for the blood test.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，sedimentation rate（沉降速率，即血沉）成为该血液检验的标准临床说法。

items.en: Not uncertain: the derivation is established. Only the first date of each technical sense is approximate, and the Indo-European root *sed- is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 并非存疑：派生关系确定。仅各技术义的首次出现年代为约数，印欧词根 *sed- 属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words resembling sedimentation but built on other roots; group two holds the processes and results it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的词；第二组是易与它混淆的过程与结果词。

entries.definition: The act of mourning aloud, from lamentari 'to wail'; it shares the -mentation shape but has nothing to do with settling.
entries.definitionCN: 指放声哀悼，来自 lamentari「哀号」；共享 -mentation 这一外形，却与沉降无关。

entries.definition: The process of reasoning in support of a claim, from argumentum; the long ending is similar, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指为支持主张而推理的过程，来自 argumentum；长词尾相似，词根不同。

entries.definition: Means calming a patient with drugs, from sedare 'to settle, calm', a causative of sedere; it is about quieting a person, not dropping particles.
entries.definitionCN: 意为用药物使病人镇静，来自 sedare「使安定」——sedere 的使动形式；它说的是让人安静，不是让颗粒落下。

entries.definition: Means incitement against authority, from sed- 'apart' plus ire 'go'; the sed- here is not the 'sit' root at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为煽动叛离权威，来自 sed-「分开」加 ire「走」；这里的 sed- 根本不是「坐」的词根。

entries.definition: The laying down of material by any agent; sedimentation is the settling of particles, one route to deposition.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何介质把物质放下的过程；sedimentation 是颗粒沉降，是沉积的一条路径。

entries.definition: The everyday word for particles coming to rest; sedimentation is its technical and geological counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 颗粒归于静止的日常说法；sedimentation 是它的技术与地质对应词。

entries.definition: A general word for increase by adding, with no image of liquid or layers.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指通过添加而增多，不含液体或层理的意象。

entries.definition: The formation of a solid from a solution by chemical reaction, whereas sedimentation is mechanical settling.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学反应使溶液析出固体，而 sedimentation 是机械沉降。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffixes, the real laboratory phrases and the real water-treatment vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的实验室说法与真实的水处理词汇。

normal.en: Sediment plus -ation: the suffix turns the material into the process.
normal.cn: sediment 加 -ation：后缀把材料变成过程。

normal.en: The laboratory phrase is sedimentation rate, and the plant phrase is sedimentation tank.
normal.cn: 实验室说法是 sedimentation rate（沉降速率），厂里说法是 sedimentation tank（沉淀池）。

normal.en: The family runs sediment, sedimentary, sedimentation, sedimentology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sediment、sedimentary、sedimentation、sedimentology。

normal.en: Coarse grains settle first, fine clay last, so a settled sample is sorted by size.
normal.cn: 粗颗粒先沉，细黏土最后沉，因此沉降后的样品按粒径分选。

normal.en: In medicine the same noun appears in the blood test called the sedimentation rate.
normal.cn: 在医学中，同一个名词出现在称为血沉的检验里。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass that never needs turning because gravity does the work.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不用翻转的沙漏，因为重力在替它工作。

abstract.en: Picture a city slowly buried by its own dust, one quiet night at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市被自己的尘埃慢慢埋住，一夜一夜地安静堆积。

abstract.en: Picture a queue where everyone eventually sits down in order of weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍，所有人最终按体重顺序坐下。

examples.en: Sedimentation in the reservoir has cut its storage capacity by a fifth.
examples.cn: 水库中的沉积已使其库容减少了五分之一。

examples.en: Engineers added a sedimentation tank before the filter beds.
examples.cn: 工程师在滤池前加了一座沉淀池。

examples.en: A high sedimentation rate can accompany infection or inflammation.
examples.cn: 血沉升高可伴随感染或炎症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞底（sedi）门（men）太（ta）深（tion）」——塞到底下、越积越深的过程 → 沉积作用

root: 拉丁 sedere「坐、安定」+ -mentum → sedimentum「沉降」；再加 -atio（动作名词后缀）→ sedimentation「沉降过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process across scales: a jar, a lake, a basin, a treatment plant, a centrifuge, a blood tube and an industrial tank all show particles losing speed and settling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程跨越不同尺度：瓶、湖、盆地、处理厂、离心机、血样管与工业沉淀池，都在演示颗粒失去速度而沉降。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a settling column in which faster grains stop lower and finer grains stop higher.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根沉降柱，快颗粒停在更低处，细颗粒停在更高处。

branches.en: SETTLING IN WATER: the jar and the treatment tank use the same physics.
branches.cn: 水中沉降：玻璃瓶与处理池遵循同一物理规律。

branches.en: GEOLOGICAL BUILD-UP: what settles today becomes a bed, and beds become rock.
branches.cn: 地质堆积：今天沉下的成为一层，层又变成岩石。

branches.en: SEPARATION: the centrifuge and the industrial tank both use settling to sort or thicken.
branches.cn: 分离：离心机与工业池都用沉降来分选或增稠。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL RATE: medicine borrows the process and turns it into a number.
branches.cn: 临床速率：医学借走这一过程，把它变成一个数值。

branches.en: THE RATE ITSELF: once measured, the process becomes a figure to compare across sites.
branches.cn: 速率本身：一旦可测，过程就成了可跨地点比较的数字。

intro.en: Sedimentation stacks three Latin pieces: a verb, a result suffix and an action suffix.
intro.cn: sedimentation 叠了三个拉丁成分：动词、结果后缀与动作后缀。

latinIntro.en: Sedere 'to sit' plus -mentum and -atio yields sedimentation; the same suffixes build monumentum and narratio.
latinIntro.cn: sedere「坐」加 -mentum 与 -atio 得到 sedimentation；同样的后缀也构成 monumentum 与 narratio。

items.example: The root states the resting position.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根陈述静止的位置。

items.example: Narratio means the act of telling.
items.exampleCN: narratio 意为讲述这一动作。
这些岩层是沉积成因的。

latinEntries.structure: sedimentatio, sedimentationis (f., third declension; late Latin)

definition_zh: 变质作用；（岩石在高温高压下的）变质；变形（比喻用法）
definition_en: the process by which heat, pressure or chemically active fluids change the minerals and texture of solid rock without melting it
core_image: 山带深处，一层页岩在压力下被压薄，原来的矿物重结晶成发亮的新颗粒
scene: 地质学生在显微镜下看一片岩石薄片，原来的颗粒已被压扁，重结晶成互相咬合的新矿物。Heat and pressure drove the metamorphism that produced this schist.
sceneCN: 这里 metamorphism 指「岩石在固态下因温度、压力或流体作用而改变矿物与结构的过程」（第 1 个义项：变质作用）；句意为高温与压力驱动了变质作用，生成了这片片岩。可辨识物件：显微镜、岩石薄片、被压扁的颗粒、互相咬合的新矿物。

senses.title: Change of rock in the solid state
senses.definition: the alteration of a rock's minerals and texture by heat and pressure while it stays solid
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石在保持固态的情况下，因温度与压力改变矿物与结构
senses.example: Heat and pressure drove the metamorphism that produced this schist.
senses.exampleCN: 高温与压力驱动了变质作用，生成了这片片岩。
senses.why: -ism marks a process, and the Greek pieces say 'change of form', exactly the solid-state recrystallization geology means.
senses.whyCN: -ism 标记过程，希腊成分意为「形态改变」，正是地质学所说的固态重结晶。

senses.title: Large-scale regional change
senses.definition: metamorphism affecting a whole region during mountain building
senses.definitionCN: 指造山过程中影响整个区域的变质作用
senses.example: Regional metamorphism turned the mudstone into schist across the range.
senses.exampleCN: 区域变质作用使整条山脉的泥岩变成了片岩。
senses.why: Mountain building affects whole regions, so regional names the scale rather than a different process.
senses.whyCN: 造山影响整个区域，因此 regional 命名的是尺度，而非另一过程。

senses.title: Change beside an intrusion
senses.definition: metamorphism caused by the heat of a nearby magma body
senses.definitionCN: 指由附近岩浆体的热量引起的变质作用
senses.example: Contact metamorphism baked the limestone into marble.
senses.exampleCN: 接触变质作用把石灰岩烘成了大理岩。
senses.why: An intrusion supplies heat locally, and the word names that setting rather than a new mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 侵入体在局部提供热量，这个词命名的是环境，而非新机制。

senses.title: Change along faults
senses.definition: metamorphism produced by shearing and crushing in fault zones
senses.definitionCN: 指断层带内剪切与破碎造成的变质作用
senses.example: Dynamic metamorphism crushed the granite into mylonite.
senses.exampleCN: 动力变质作用把花岗岩碾成了糜棱岩。
senses.why: Fault movement supplies shear, a mechanical route to the same result.
senses.whyCN: 断层运动提供剪切，这是一种通向同一结果的机械途径。

senses.title: Change by impact
senses.definition: metamorphism caused by the shock wave of a meteorite impact
senses.definitionCN: 指由陨石撞击的冲击波造成的变质作用
senses.example: Shock metamorphism left cone-shaped fractures in the quartz.
senses.exampleCN: 冲击变质在石英里留下了锥状裂隙。
senses.why: An impact supplies a shock wave, the most extreme and briefest route to the same change.
senses.whyCN: 撞击提供冲击波，这是通向同一变化最极端也最短暂的途径。

senses.title: Change during deep burial or hot fluids
senses.titleCN: 深埋或热流体造成的变质
senses.definition: metamorphism from deep burial or from hot mineral-rich fluids moving through rock
senses.definitionCN: 指深埋或富矿物流体穿过岩石造成的变质作用
senses.example: Hydrothermal metamorphism deposited new minerals along the veins.
senses.exampleCN: 热液变质沿裂隙沉积出新矿物。
senses.why: Burial and hot fluids supply heat and chemistry without mountain building.
senses.whyCN: 深埋与热流体在不造山的情况下提供热与化学条件。

senses.title: The degree or grade reached
senses.definition: the level of metamorphism reached, from low grade to high grade
senses.definitionCN: 指变质达到的级别，从低级到高级
senses.example: Low-grade metamorphism only slightly altered the shale.
senses.exampleCN: 低级变质只轻微改变了这片页岩。
senses.why: Grade measures how far the process has gone, turning a process into a scale.
senses.whyCN: 级别度量过程推进到何种程度，把过程变成了一把尺。

senses.title: Figurative change of form
senses.titleCN: 比喻：形态或性质的彻底改变
senses.definition: figurative: a complete change in form or character, as if one substance became another
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：形态或性质彻底改变，仿佛一种物质变成了另一种
senses.example: The novel describes the metamorphism of a village into a suburb.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描写一个村庄如何变形为郊区。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the idea of form changing while the substance remains.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了「形态在变、实体仍在」这一核心想法。

intro.en: Metamorphism is built on Greek meta- 'change' and morphē 'form', with the English suffix -ism marking a process or system.
intro.cn: metamorphism 由希腊 meta-「变化」与 morphē「形状」构成，英语后缀 -ism 标记过程或体系。

items.en: Metamorphē 'transformation' was formed from meta- 'change, beyond' plus morphē 'form' and was used of changes of shape in myth and nature.
items.cn: metamorphē「变形」由 meta-「变化、超出」加 morphē「形状」构成，在神话与自然描写中指形态改变。

items.en: The verb metamorphoun 'to transform' supplied the action behind the noun, and it passed into Latin as metamorphosis, a Greek loan.
items.cn: 动词 metamorphoun「使变形」提供了名词背后的动作，并以 metamorphosis 这一希腊借词形式进入拉丁语。

items.en: -ismos in Greek and -ismus in Latin named a practice, process or system; English -ism does the same, so metamorphism names the process rather than one transformed object.
items.cn: 希腊 -ismos 与拉丁 -ismus 命名实践、过程或体系；英语 -ism 作用相同，因此 metamorphism 命名的是过程，而不是某个被变形的对象。

items.en: Geologists adopted the word in the nineteenth century for solid-state change of rock, distinguishing it from melting and from simple weathering.
items.cn: 地质学家在十九世纪采用这个词指岩石的固态变化，以区别于熔融与单纯风化。

items.en: Regional, contact, dynamic, shock and hydrothermal metamorphism later became standard subdivisions named by their setting.
items.cn: 区域、接触、动力、冲击与热液变质后来成为按环境划分的标准类型。

items.en: Source generally regarded as established through Greek, but the origin of morphē 'form' itself is uncertain, and the exact first English use in geology is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源一般认为是可溯至希腊语，但 morphē「形状」本身的来源不确定，且该词在地质学中首次出现的准确年代无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on meta- and morph- that are easily confused; group two holds neighbouring geological processes.
note.cn: 第一组是由 meta- 与 morph- 构成、易混的词；第二组是相邻的地质过程。

entries.definition: Names one complete change of form, as of a caterpillar into a butterfly; metamorphism names the geological process as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次完整的形态改变，如毛虫变成蝴蝶；metamorphism 把地质过程作为整体来命名。

entries.definition: The adjective describing rock or a process of this kind; it shares the root and differs only in word class.
entries.definitionCN: 描述此类岩石或过程的形容词；共享词根，只差词类。

entries.definition: From meta- 'across' plus pherein 'to carry': carrying meaning across; the morph- element is absent, so the resemblance is only in the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 meta-「跨越」加 pherein「携带」：把意义搬运过去；其中没有 morph- 成分，相似只在前缀上。

entries.definition: Means without regular form, from a- 'not' plus morphē; it is the opposite of having a definite crystalline form.
entries.definitionCN: 意为无定形的，来自 a-「不」加 morphē；与具有确定晶形相对。

entries.definition: The growth of new crystals in the solid state; it is how metamorphism usually changes a rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指固态下新晶体的生长；变质作用通常正是通过它改变岩石。

entries.definition: Metamorphism accompanied by a marked change in bulk chemistry through migrating fluids; it is a special kind of metamorphism.
entries.definitionCN: 指伴随流体迁移造成整体化学成分明显变化的变质；它是变质作用的一个特殊类型。

entries.definition: The low-temperature alteration of sediment into rock, before metamorphism begins.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉积物在变质作用开始之前、低温下变成岩石的变化。

entries.definition: The breakdown of rock at the surface by water, air and organisms, which is not metamorphism because pressure and heat are absent.
entries.definitionCN: 指岩石在地表受水、空气与生物作用而崩解；由于缺少高温高压，它不算变质作用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek pieces and the real subdivision names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊语成分与真实的分类名称。

normal.en: Meta- 'change' plus morphē 'form': a change of form inside solid rock.
normal.cn: meta-「变化」加 morphē「形状」：固态岩石内部的形态改变。

normal.en: The subdivisions are named by setting: regional, contact, dynamic, shock, hydrothermal.
normal.cn: 分类按环境命名：区域、接触、动力、冲击、热液。

normal.en: Metamorphism stops short of melting; melt it and you get igneous rock instead.
normal.cn: 变质作用止于熔融之前；一旦熔化，得到的就是火成岩。

normal.en: The family runs metamorphic, metamorphose, metamorphosis, metamorphosed.
normal.cn: 词族包括 metamorphic、metamorphose、metamorphosis、metamorphosed。

normal.en: Grade runs low to high: shale, slate, schist, gneiss.
normal.cn: 变质程度由低到高：页岩、板岩、片岩、片麻岩。

abstract.en: Picture a book rewritten in a foreign alphabet without changing the pages.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书只换了字体、纸页却没换。

abstract.en: Picture pressure as a sculptor who works without heat enough to melt.
abstract.cn: 想象压力是一位不用足够高温就能雕刻的雕塑家。

abstract.en: Picture a caterpillar that never becomes a butterfly but only a harder caterpillar.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毛虫不变成蝴蝶，只变成更硬的毛虫。

examples.en: Regional metamorphism accompanies the growth of mountain belts.
examples.cn: 区域变质伴随山脉的生长。

examples.en: The marble formed by contact metamorphism around a granite intrusion.
examples.cn: 大理岩由花岗岩侵入体周围的接触变质形成。

examples.en: Shock metamorphism is recognized by features that only an impact can produce.
examples.cn: 冲击变质可通过只有撞击才能产生的特征来识别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米塔（meta）摸夫（morph）ism」——形状被换了一遍 → 变质作用

root: 希腊 meta-「变化、超出」+ morphē「形状」+ -ismos（过程名词后缀）→ metamorphē「变形」；经拉丁 metamorphosis 进入欧洲语言，英语加 -ism 指固体岩石的变质过程。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process under different conditions: the same solid-state recrystallization appears regionally, near an intrusion, along a fault, under an impact, in deep burial and at different grades, before the word is finally used for change in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程在不同条件下出现：同样的固态重结晶依次出现在区域、侵入体旁、断层带、撞击下、深埋中，并呈现不同级别，最后才被用于一般意义上的改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: solid rock remade from inside, its grains crushed and regrown without ever melting.
core.cn: 核心意象：固态岩石从内部被重造，颗粒被压碎又重新长出，全程不曾熔化。

branches.en: THE GENERAL AND THE REGIONAL: one rock or a whole range, the mechanism is the same.
branches.cn: 一般与区域：一块岩石或整条山脉，机制相同。

branches.en: HEAT AND FLUIDS: an intrusion bakes its neighbour, and hot fluids rewrite veins.
branches.cn: 热与流体：侵入体烘烤邻居，热液改写矿脉。

branches.en: MECHANICAL SHOCK: shearing along faults and the blast of an impact both crush grains.
branches.cn: 机械冲击：断层剪切与撞击爆破都在碾碎颗粒。

branches.en: GRADE: the same process measured by how far it has gone.
branches.cn: 级别：同一过程按推进程度来度量。

branches.en: IMAGE: change of form leaves geology and becomes a figure for any deep transformation.
branches.cn: 意象：形态改变离开地质学，成为任何深刻转变的比喻。

intro.en: Metamorphism is three Greek pieces plus an English suffix, and each piece also builds other English words.
intro.cn: metamorphism 是三个希腊成分加一个英语后缀，每个成分还构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Greek morphē 'form' reached Latin chiefly through the loanword metamorphosis; Latin itself has no native relative, so the entries below are marked as Greek loans.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 morphē「形状」主要通过借词 metamorphosis 进入拉丁语；拉丁语本身没有本土同族词，因此以下条目标注为希腊借词。

items.exampleCN: 变质岩显示出新的颗粒。

items.example: The metamorphosed bed is now gneiss.
items.exampleCN: 变质的岩层如今是片麻岩。

definition_zh: 矿物学；（岩石或标本的）矿物组成
definition_en: the scientific study of minerals, or the mineral composition of a rock or specimen
core_image: 标本柜前，一块花岗岩被切开，石英、长石与云母各自显出不同的光泽与颜色
scene: 标本柜前，讲解员把一块含石英与长石的岩石切开，逐项说明其中的矿物种类与比例。The mineralogy of the granite is dominated by quartz and feldspar.
sceneCN: 这里 mineralogy 指「岩石或标本中矿物的种类与组成」（第 2 个义项：某个样品的矿物组成）；句意为这块花岗岩的矿物组成以石英与长石为主。可辨识物件：标本柜、切开的花岗岩、石英、长石、云母片。

senses.title: The science of minerals
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies the composition, structure and properties of minerals
senses.definitionCN: 指研究矿物成分、结构与性质的学科分支
senses.example: She studied mineralogy before turning to petrology.
senses.exampleCN: 她在转向岩石学之前先学了矿物学。
senses.why: -logy names a discipline, and the base names its object, so the word is transparent by construction.
senses.whyCN: -logy 命名学科，词基命名对象，因此这个词在构词上一目了然。

senses.title: Mineral composition of a sample
senses.definition: the kinds and proportions of minerals present in a rock or specimen
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石或标本中矿物的种类与比例
senses.example: The mineralogy of the granite is dominated by quartz and feldspar.
senses.exampleCN: 这块花岗岩的矿物组成以石英与长石为主。
senses.why: The same noun also answers 'what is this rock made of', a question about composition rather than about a science.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也回答「这块岩石由什么组成」，这是关于成分的问题，而非关于学科。

senses.title: Descriptive mineralogy
senses.definition: the branch that names, describes and classifies minerals
senses.definitionCN: 指对矿物进行命名、描述与分类的分支
senses.example: Descriptive mineralogy lists hardness, lustre and cleavage.
senses.exampleCN: 描述矿物学列出硬度、光泽与解理。
senses.why: Description is the first task of any natural science, so the branch has its own name.
senses.whyCN: 描述是任何博物科学的第一项任务，因此这一分支有自己的名称。

senses.title: Optical mineralogy
senses.definition: the study of minerals in thin section under polarized light
senses.definitionCN: 指在偏光下用薄片研究矿物的方法
senses.example: Optical mineralogy identifies grains by their interference colours.
senses.exampleCN: 光性矿物学依据干涉色鉴定颗粒。
senses.why: The microscope turned minerals into optical objects and created a method-based branch.
senses.whyCN: 显微镜把矿物变成光学对象，从而造出一个以方法为基础的分支。

senses.title: Determinative mineralogy
senses.definition: the practical identification of unknown minerals by physical and chemical tests
senses.definitionCN: 指通过物理与化学试验鉴定未知矿物的实务
senses.example: Determinative mineralogy relies on streak and hardness.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴定矿物学依靠条痕与硬度。
senses.why: Identification is practical work, and its tests gave the branch a name.
senses.whyCN: 鉴定是务实的工作，其试验方法给这一分支带来了名称。

senses.title: Economic and applied mineralogy
senses.definition: the study of ore and industrial minerals with a view to their use
senses.definitionCN: 指以利用为目的研究矿石与工业矿物
senses.example: Economic mineralogy assessed the clay deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 经济矿物学评估了这处黏土矿床。
senses.why: Ores and industrial minerals give the science an economic application, and the adjective marks it.
senses.whyCN: 矿石与工业矿物给这门科学带来经济应用，形容词标记的正是这一层。

senses.title: Mineralogy of a region or occurrence
senses.titleCN: 某地区或矿点的矿物组成
senses.definition: the mineral assemblage characteristic of a district or deposit
senses.definitionCN: 指某一地区或矿床特有的矿物组合
senses.example: The mineralogy of the district includes rare borates.
senses.exampleCN: 该区的矿物组合包含稀有的硼酸盐。
senses.why: A district's assemblage is a local instance of the science, so the noun can mean 'the mineralogy of a place'.
senses.whyCN: 某区的矿物组合是这门科学的地方实例，因此名词可指「某地的矿物组成」。

senses.title: A systematic account of minerals
senses.definition: a treatise or systematic account setting out the known minerals
senses.definitionCN: 指系统论述已知矿物的著作
senses.example: The old mineralogy described three hundred species.
senses.exampleCN: 那部古老的矿物学著作描述了三百个矿物种。
senses.why: A systematic book is the science in written form, and the noun can name the book itself.
senses.whyCN: 系统性的书是这门科学的书面形态，名词也可直接指这本书。

intro.en: Mineralogy joins mineral, a word of uncertain medieval origin, to the Greek-derived suffix -logy 'study of'.
intro.cn: mineralogy 把来源不确定的中世纪词 mineral 与希腊来源的后缀 -logy「……学」组合起来。

items.en: Minera 'ore, mine' appears in medieval Latin; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it may come from Old French miniere 'mine' or from a pre-Roman term.
items.cn: minera「矿石、矿」见于中世纪拉丁语；其更深来源不确定，可能来自古法语 miniere「矿」，也可能来自罗马之前的用语。

items.en: The adjective mineralis 'pertaining to mines' produced English mineral, first as a general word for something dug from the earth.
items.cn: 形容词 mineralis「与矿有关的」产生英语 mineral，最初泛指从地下挖出的东西。

items.en: Latin -logia and Greek -logia 'study, account' come from logos 'word, reason'; English -logy forms the names of disciplines.
items.cn: 拉丁 -logia 与希腊 -logia「研究、论述」来自 logos「言词、理」；英语 -logy 构成学科名称。

items.en: Mineralogy appears in the seventeenth century as the name of the new descriptive science of minerals, alongside the older word mineralist.
items.cn: mineralogy 在十七世纪出现，作为新兴的描述性矿物科学的名称，与更早的 mineralist 并用。

items.en: Optical, determinative and economic mineralogy later split off as named subfields, and the word also came to mean the mineral makeup of a specimen.
items.cn: 光性、鉴定与经济矿物学后来分化为有名称的子领域，这个词也开始指标本的矿物组成。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the origin of minera is unsettled, and no Latin verb or adjective can be shown to be its base; any pre-Roman reconstruction is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根部分）：minera 的来源没有定论，无法证明某个拉丁动词或形容词是它的基础；任何罗马之前的重构均属假说。

note.en: Group one holds -logy words and mineral words that look alike; group two holds neighbouring Earth-science disciplines.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的 -logy 词与矿物词；第二组是相邻的地球科学学科。

entries.definition: The substance itself, not the study of it; mineralogy is the discipline built on this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿物这一物质本身，而非对它的研究；mineralogy 是在这个名词上建立的学科。

entries.definition: The technology of extracting and working metals, with -ourgia 'working' rather than -logia 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 指提炼与加工金属的技术，后缀是 -ourgia「加工」而非 -logia「研究」。

entries.definition: The study of rocks as wholes, from Greek petra 'rock'; it uses mineralogy but does not replace it.
entries.definitionCN: 指把岩石作为整体来研究，来自希腊 petra「岩石」；它使用矿物学但不取代它。

entries.definition: A specialist in minerals; it shares the discipline's root but names a person rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿物研究者；共享学科词根，但命名的是人而非领域。

entries.definition: The descriptive branch that names and classifies rocks, from Greek graphein 'to write'.
entries.definitionCN: 指对岩石进行命名与分类的描述性分支，来自希腊 graphein「书写」。

entries.definition: The study of crystal structure and form, closely allied to mineralogy but focused on the lattice.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究晶体结构与形态的学科，与矿物学紧密相关，但聚焦于晶格。

entries.definition: The study of the chemical composition of rocks and minerals; mineralogy supplies the species, geochemistry the elements.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究岩石与矿物化学成分的学科；矿物学提供矿物种，地球化学提供元素。

entries.definition: The study of gemstones as materials of value, narrower than mineralogy and market-oriented.
entries.definitionCN: 指把宝石作为贵重材料来研究，比矿物学窄，且面向市场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real subfields and the real companion disciplines.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的子领域与真实的伴生学科。

normal.en: Mineral plus -logy: the study of minerals, exactly as the Greek suffix says.
normal.cn: mineral 加 -logy：正如希腊后缀所示，对矿物的研究。

normal.en: Named subfields: optical, descriptive, determinative, economic mineralogy.
normal.cn: 有名子领域：光性、描述、鉴定、经济矿物学。

normal.en: The trio is mineralogy, petrology, geochemistry, from species to rock to element.
normal.cn: 三者是矿物学、岩石学、地球化学，从矿物种到岩石再到元素。

normal.en: The family runs mineral, mineralogy, mineralogist, mineralogical.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mineral、mineralogy、mineralogist、mineralogical。

normal.en: Hardness, lustre and cleavage are the three questions descriptive mineralogy asks first.
normal.cn: 硬度、光泽与解理是描述矿物学最先问的三个问题。

abstract.en: Picture a library that catalogues every kind of stone by its smallest readable unit.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，按石头最小的可读单位来编目。

abstract.en: Picture a jeweller's loupe that turns a rock into a list of ingredients.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜把一块岩石变成一张成分表。

abstract.en: Picture the earth's crust written in a vocabulary of minerals.
abstract.cn: 想象地壳用一种矿物词汇写成。

examples.en: Mineralogy describes how atoms are arranged in each mineral species.
examples.cn: 矿物学描述每个矿物种中原子如何排列。

examples.en: The mineralogy of the ash points to a basaltic source.
examples.cn: 这些火山灰的矿物组成指向玄武质来源。

examples.en: She taught optical mineralogy to second-year geology students.
examples.cn: 她给地质专业二年级学生讲授光性矿物学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你（mine）若（ral）乐基（ogy）」——研究小矿石的学问 → 矿物学

root: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石、矿」（更深来源不确定）+ 希腊 -logia「研究、论述」（来自 logos「言词、理」）→ mineralogy「矿物学」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one science outward: it begins as a discipline, then narrows to a specimen's makeup, then splits into descriptive, optical, determinative and economic branches, then wideens to a district and finally to a written account.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一门学科向外展开：它先是学科，再收窄到标本的组成，然后分为描述、光性、鉴定、经济各分支，再扩展到地区，最后成为成书的论述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut rock in which each mineral shows its own colour and lustre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块切开的岩石，每种矿物显出各自的颜色与光泽。

branches.en: FROM DISCIPLINE TO SAMPLE: the science and the specimen's makeup share one vocabulary.
branches.cn: 从学科到样品：学科与标本组成共享一套词汇。

branches.en: DESCRIBE AND SEE: naming by properties and identifying under polarized light.
branches.cn: 描述与观察：按性质命名，在偏光下鉴定。

branches.en: IDENTIFY: tests of streak and hardness turn an unknown grain into a name.
branches.cn: 鉴定：条痕与硬度试验把未知颗粒变成名称。

branches.en: WHERE AND FOR WHAT: economic use and district assemblages apply the science to ground and market.
branches.cn: 何处与何用：经济利用与地区组合把学科用于地面与市场。

branches.en: THE BOOK: the subject becomes a systematic written account.
branches.cn: 成书：学科成为系统的书面论述。

intro.en: Mineralogy joins an uncertain medieval noun to a Greek suffix, so only the suffix can be read with certainty.
intro.cn: mineralogy 把一个来源不确定的中世纪名词与希腊后缀组合，因此只有后缀可以确定地读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin minera 'ore' and mineralis 'of mines' supply the first element; Latin -logia, from Greek -logia and logos, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 minera「矿石」与 mineralis「矿的」提供第一成分；拉丁 -logia（来自希腊 -logia 与 logos）提供第二成分。

items.exampleCN: minera 提供了词族的基础。

items.meaning: a substance dug from the earth
items.meaningCN: 从地下采出的物质；矿物
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石含有数种矿物。

items.example: Biology is the study of life.

items.exampleCN: logos 支撑整个 -logy 词族。

items.example: Mineralogy began as a descriptive science.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学起初是一门描述性科学。

items.example: The mineralogist named the new species.

随后做了一次矿物学调查。
这些岩层在矿物学上相似。

items.meaning: a substance like a mineral but not crystalline
items.exampleCN: 黑曜岩是一种似矿物物质。
