mineralogia, mineralogiae (f., first declension; modern Latin coinage)

definition_zh: 矿物学的；与矿物组成有关的
definition_en: relating to mineralogy or to the mineral composition of a rock or specimen
core_image: 岩芯箱旁，研究员把薄片放到显微镜下，记录各矿物的种类与含量比例
scene: 岩芯箱旁，研究员把薄片放到显微镜下，逐项记录各矿物的种类与含量比例。A mineralogical analysis showed quartz, mica and feldspar in nearly equal parts.
sceneCN: 这里 mineralogical 指「与矿物学或矿物组成有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于矿物学范畴的）；句意为一次矿物学分析显示石英、云母与长石几乎等量。可辨识物件：岩芯箱、薄片、显微镜、记录表。

senses.title: Relating to mineralogy
senses.definition: of or belonging to the science of minerals
senses.definitionCN: 指属于或关于矿物学的
senses.example: A mineralogical analysis showed quartz, mica and feldspar in nearly equal parts.
senses.exampleCN: 一次矿物学分析显示石英、云母与长石几乎等量。
senses.why: -ical turns the discipline into an adjective, exactly as geological does for geology.
senses.whyCN: -ical 把学科变成形容词，正如 geological 之于 geology。

senses.title: Relating to mineral composition
senses.definition: concerning the kinds and proportions of minerals in a material
senses.definitionCN: 指关于材料中矿物的种类与比例的
senses.example: The mineralogical composition changes across the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿物组成在整层中逐渐变化。
senses.why: Composition is the question this adjective most often answers in reports.
senses.whyCN: 在报告里，这个形容词最常回答的就是成分问题。

senses.title: Based on analytical methods
senses.definition: of a method: using microscopy, diffraction or chemical tests on minerals
senses.definitionCN: 指方法上采用显微、衍射或化学试验研究矿物
senses.example: A mineralogical study used X-ray diffraction.
senses.exampleCN: 一项矿物学研究使用了射线衍射。
senses.why: Methods define a branch, so analytical work done with them is called mineralogical.
senses.whyCN: 方法定义一个分支，用这些方法做的分析工作便称为矿物学的。

senses.title: Belonging to a research programme
senses.definition: of work: carried out within mineralogy as a discipline
senses.definitionCN: 指作为矿物学学科内的研究工作
senses.example: The mineralogical survey took three seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这项矿物学调查用了三个野外季。
senses.why: A project carried out under the discipline takes the adjective as its label.
senses.whyCN: 在学科之下开展的项目用这个形容词作标签。

senses.title: Used in classification
senses.definition: of a scheme: grouping materials by their mineral content
senses.definitionCN: 指按矿物含量对材料进行分组的方案
senses.example: The mineralogical classification separates the ash beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这套矿物学分类把各层火山灰分开。
senses.why: Classification schemes are built from mineral content, so they are mineralogical schemes.
senses.whyCN: 分类方案建立在矿物含量上，因此它们是矿物学方案。

senses.title: Characteristic of a material
senses.definition: of features: the distinctive mineral traits of a specimen
senses.definitionCN: 指标本在矿物方面有辨识度的特征
senses.example: Its mineralogical character points to a hydrothermal origin.
senses.exampleCN: 它的矿物学特征指向热液成因。
senses.why: Character is the sum of traits that identify a specimen's origin.
senses.whyCN: 特征是识别标本成因的一组性状总和。

senses.title: Belonging to a collection
senses.definition: of a collection: organized around mineral specimens
senses.definitionCN: 指围绕矿物标本组织的收藏
senses.example: The mineralogical museum keeps ten thousand specimens.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿物学博物馆收藏了一万件标本。
senses.why: Collections are organized by the same discipline, hence the mineralogical museum.
senses.whyCN: 收藏按同一学科组织，因此有矿物学博物馆。

senses.title: Belonging to a province or occurrence
senses.definition: of a district: defined by its characteristic mineral assemblage
senses.definitionCN: 指以特征矿物组合定义的地区
senses.example: The mineralogical province is known for its pegmatites.
senses.exampleCN: 这个矿物区以伟晶岩著称。
senses.why: A province is a region defined by its assemblage, so the adjective can mark a whole district.
senses.whyCN: 矿物区由矿物组合定义的地区，因此这个形容词可标记整个区域。

intro.en: Mineralogical is mineralogy with the Latin-derived adjective ending -ical, added to turn a discipline into a description.
intro.cn: mineralogical 是 mineralogy 加上拉丁来源的形容词后缀 -ical，把学科名变成描述词。

items.en: Medieval Latin minera 'ore' (origin uncertain) and mineralis 'of mines' produced mineral and then mineralogy.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石」（来源不确定）与 mineralis「矿的」产生 mineral，继而产生 mineralogy。

items.en: The suffix -logia 'study, account', from logos 'word, reason', entered Latin and then English as -logy.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia「研究、论述」来自 logos「言词、理」，进入拉丁语后再以 -logy 进入英语。

items.en: The Latin adjectival ending -icus, itself from Greek -ikos, means 'belonging to or typical of', and appears in English as -ic and -ical.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词词尾 -icus（源自希腊 -ikos）意为「属于……的、具有……特征的」，在英语中作 -ic 与 -ical。

items.en: English often keeps both -ic and -ical, as in historic and historical; mineralogical is the established adjective for the discipline.
items.cn: 英语常同时保留 -ic 与 -ical，如 historic 与 historical；mineralogical 是该学科既定的形容词形式。

items.en: The adjective spread with the growth of analytical geology, in phrases such as mineralogical composition and mineralogical analysis.
items.cn: 这个形容词随分析地质学的成长而传播，见于 mineralogical composition（矿物组成）与 mineralogical analysis（矿物学分析）等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first element only): the origin of minera remains unsettled, while the suffixal derivation through -logia and -icus is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅第一成分）：minera 的来源仍无定论，而经 -logia 与 -icus 的后缀派生是确定的。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns that resemble mineralogical; group two holds adjectives used in the same analytical reports.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似 mineralogical 的词；第二组是同类分析报告中使用的形容词。

entries.definition: The substance or a plain adjective 'of minerals'; mineralogical adds the sense of the discipline or a full composition study.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿物这一物质，或「矿物的」这一朴素形容词；mineralogical 增加学科或完整组成研究的意思。

entries.definition: Relating to the extraction and working of metals, built on -ourgia 'working', not on -logia 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 指与金属提炼和加工有关，建立在 -ourgia「加工」而非 -logia「研究」之上。

entries.definition: Relating to geology as a whole; mineralogical is the narrower adjective for the mineral branch.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个地质学有关；mineralogical 是矿物分支更窄的形容词。

entries.definition: A rarer variant using -ic instead of -ical; both exist, but mineralogical is the usual form in modern writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使用 -ic 而非 -ical 的较罕见变体；两者都存在，但现代写作中常用 mineralogical。

entries.definition: Relating to the study of rocks as wholes; mineralogical concerns their mineral parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指与把岩石作为整体的研究有关；mineralogical 关注其中的矿物部分。

entries.definition: Relating to chemical composition; a chemical analysis gives elements, a mineralogical one gives mineral species.
entries.definitionCN: 指与化学成分有关；化学分析给出元素，矿物学分析给出矿物种。

entries.definition: Relating to the arrangement and size of grains; mineralogical names what the grains are made of.
entries.definitionCN: 指与颗粒排列与大小有关；mineralogical 命名颗粒由什么构成。

entries.definition: Relating to crystal structure and symmetry rather than to mineral identity.
entries.definitionCN: 指与晶体结构和对称性有关，而非矿物种类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain and the real report phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链与真实的报告说法。

normal.en: Mineralogy plus -ical: the adjective form of the discipline, like geological from geology.
normal.cn: mineralogy 加 -ical：学科的形容词形式，如 geological 来自 geology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mineralogical analysis, mineralogical composition, mineralogical classification.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：矿物学分析、矿物组成、矿物学分类。

normal.en: The suffix chain is -logia then -icus, giving -logical in English.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 -logia 再到 -icus，在英语中成为 -logical。

normal.en: The family runs mineral, mineralogy, mineralogist, mineralogical, mineralogically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mineral、mineralogy、mineralogist、mineralogical、mineralogically。

normal.en: In a report, mineralogical answers 'what minerals', chemical answers 'what elements'.
normal.cn: 在报告里，mineralogical 回答「有哪些矿物」，chemical 回答「有哪些元素」。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass that turns a rock into an inventory list.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜把岩石变成一张清单。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a specimen that names its ingredients, not its weight.
abstract.cn: 想象标本上的标签写的是成分，不是重量。

abstract.en: Picture a dictionary entry for a stone, written in mineral names.
abstract.cn: 想象一条用矿物名写成的石头词条。

examples.en: The mineralogical composition of the sand is almost pure quartz.
examples.cn: 这些砂的矿物组成几乎是纯石英。

examples.en: A mineralogical study identified three distinct clay phases.
examples.cn: 一项矿物学研究识别出三种不同的黏土相。

examples.en: The museum's mineralogical collection fills two floors.
examples.cn: 该馆的矿物学收藏占了两层楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你（mine）若（ral）logic（逻辑）」——用逻辑研究小矿石的 → 矿物学的

root: mineral（中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石」，更深来源不确定）+ -logy（希腊 -logia「研究」）+ -ical（拉丁 -icus，源自希腊 -ikos）→ mineralogical「矿物学的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective through the work of a mineralogist: the discipline, the composition, the method, the project, the classification, the trait, the collection and the district.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个形容词走过矿物学家的工作：学科、组成、方法、项目、分类、特征、收藏与地区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin section under a microscope, each grain labelled with its mineral name.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下的一片薄片，每颗颗粒都标着矿物名。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE AND THE SAMPLE: what belongs to mineralogy is also what describes a specimen's makeup.
branches.cn: 学科与样品：属于矿物学的东西，也正是描述标本组成的东西。

branches.en: WORK DONE: analytical methods and a research programme both put the adjective into practice.
branches.cn: 所做的工作：分析方法与研究项目都把该形容词落到实处。

branches.en: NAME AND TRAIT: classification sorts materials, and character identifies their origin.
branches.cn: 名称与特征：分类把材料分开，特征指明其成因。

branches.en: THE COLLECTION: specimens are gathered and organized under the same adjective.
branches.cn: 收藏：标本在同一形容词下被收集与整理。

branches.en: THE DISTRICT: a whole region can be described by its mineral assemblage.
branches.cn: 地区：整个区域可按其矿物组合来描述。

intro.en: Mineralogical is a three-piece word: an uncertain noun, a Greek study suffix and a Latin adjective ending.
intro.cn: mineralogical 由三部分组成：一个来源不确定的名词、一个希腊研究后缀与一个拉丁形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin minera and mineralis give the base; Latin -logia (from Greek) gives the discipline; Latin -icus (from Greek -ikos) gives the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 minera 与 mineralis 提供词基；拉丁 -logia（源自希腊）提供学科；拉丁 -icus（源自希腊 -ikos）提供形容词词尾。

items.example: Minera is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: minera 是整个词族的词基。
这个后缀命名一门学科。
矿物学描述矿物种与结构。
geological 意为属于地质学的。
这些火山灰在矿物学上均一。

items.example: Opal is classed as a mineraloid.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白石被归为似矿物物质。

latinEntries.structure: minera, minerae (f., first declension; medieval Latin, origin uncertain)

definition_zh: 晶体；水晶；晶质玻璃；（仪表中的）石英元件
definition_en: a solid whose atoms are arranged in a regular repeating pattern, or a clear piece of such material, especially quartz
core_image: 展柜里一块透明六棱柱矿石在灯下折出细碎光点，六个平面各映一小片白光
scene: 博物馆展柜里，一块透明六棱柱形的矿石在灯光下折出细碎的光点。The crystal grew in a cavity and kept its six flat faces.
sceneCN: 这里 crystal 指「具有规则内部结构、外形平整的晶体」（第 1 个义项：原子规则排列的固体，尤指天然晶形完好的矿物）；句意为这块晶体在晶洞里生长，保留了六个平整晶面。可辨识物件：展柜、透明六棱柱、灯光折射、平整晶面。

pos.zh: 晶体；水晶；晶质玻璃；石英元件
水晶的；透明的（多用于固定搭配）

senses.title: Solid with a regular atomic lattice
senses.definition: a solid in which atoms or ions are arranged in a repeating three-dimensional pattern
senses.definitionCN: 指原子或离子按三维重复图案排列的固体
senses.example: The crystal grew in a cavity and kept its six flat faces.
senses.exampleCN: 这块晶体在晶洞里生长，保留了六个平整晶面。
senses.why: The definition of a crystal is internal order, not outer shape; the lattice is what makes flat faces possible.
senses.whyCN: 晶体的定义是内部秩序而非外形；正是晶格使平整晶面成为可能。

senses.title: A natural mineral specimen
senses.definition: a naturally grown piece of a mineral with flat faces, especially quartz
senses.definitionCN: 指天然生长、具有平整晶面的矿物，尤指石英
senses.example: A clear crystal from the Alps stood on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上摆着一块来自阿尔卑斯山的透明晶体。
senses.why: Natural specimens are the word's oldest referent, and clear quartz is its type.
senses.whyCN: 天然标本是这个词最古老的所指，而透明石英是它的典型。

senses.title: Crystal glass
senses.definition: heavy, clear glass containing lead oxide, used for fine tableware
senses.definitionCN: 指含氧化铅的厚重透明玻璃，用于精致器皿
senses.example: The decanter is made of cut crystal.
senses.exampleCN: 这只醒酒器由晶质玻璃磨制而成。
senses.why: Lead glass was named for its clarity and weight, borrowing the stone's name.
senses.whyCN: 铅玻璃因清澈与厚重而得名，借用了石头的名字。

senses.title: Objects made of such glass
senses.definition: articles such as glasses, bowls or chandeliers made of crystal glass
senses.definitionCN: 指用晶质玻璃制成的杯、碗或吊灯等物件
senses.example: The chandelier's crystals chimed in the draught.
senses.exampleCN: 吊灯上的水晶挂件在穿堂风里叮当作响。
senses.why: Once the material has a name, objects made of it inherit the name.
senses.whyCN: 材料一旦有了名字，用它制成的器物便继承这个名字。

senses.title: Quartz element in instruments
senses.definition: a thin quartz plate used to keep time or frequency in electronic circuits
senses.definitionCN: 指电子电路中用于计时或稳频的石英薄片
senses.example: The watch keeps time with a tiny crystal.
senses.exampleCN: 这只表靠一块微小的石英晶体计时。
senses.why: A quartz plate keeps frequency steady, so the stone's name moved into electronics.
senses.whyCN: 石英薄片能稳定频率，于是石头的名字进入了电子学。

senses.title: Ice crystal
senses.definition: a small particle of ice with a regular shape, as in snow or clouds
senses.definitionCN: 指形状规则的微小冰粒，如雪花或云中的冰晶
senses.example: Snow is made of countless ice crystals.
senses.exampleCN: 雪由无数冰晶构成。
senses.why: Ice crystals show the same lattice at a scale you can hold in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 冰晶在手掌尺度上展示了同样的晶格。

senses.title: Crystal ball
senses.definition: a glass or crystal sphere used by fortune-tellers, or a metaphor for prediction
senses.definitionCN: 指占卜者用的玻璃或水晶球，也比喻预测能力
senses.example: No crystal ball can tell how the market will move.
senses.exampleCN: 没有水晶球能预知市场走向。
senses.why: A crystal ball turns transparency into a claim of foresight.
senses.whyCN: 水晶球把透明变成一种关于预见的宣称。

senses.title: A grain of crystallized sugar or salt
senses.definition: one grain of a substance that has solidified into a regular shape
senses.definitionCN: 指固结成规则形状的一粒物质
senses.example: Stir until the sugar crystals dissolve.
senses.exampleCN: 搅拌到糖粒完全溶解。
senses.why: Sugar and salt grains are small crystals, so the everyday sense follows from the technical one.
senses.whyCN: 糖粒与盐粒都是小晶体，日常义正是从技术义延伸而来。

senses.title: Clear, transparent quality
senses.definition: figurative or literary: the clearness of water, air or sound
senses.definitionCN: 比喻或文学用法：水、空气或声音的清澈
senses.example: We swam in the crystal of the mountain lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山湖的清透水中游泳。
senses.why: Clarity is the optical effect of order, and the word extends to anything perfectly clear.
senses.whyCN: 清澈是有序在光学上的效果，这个词于是扩展到任何极为透明之物。

intro.en: Crystal goes back to a Greek word for ice, applied first to clear quartz because it looked like permanently frozen water.
intro.cn: crystal 可上溯到希腊语表示「冰」的词，最初用于透明石英，因为它看起来像永不融化的水。

items.en: Krystallos meant 'ice' and also 'rock crystal', the clear quartz believed to be ice frozen so hard that it never melted.
items.cn: krystallos 意为「冰」，也指「水晶」——那种被认为冻得极硬、永不融化的透明石英。

items.en: Kryos 'frost, icy cold' is generally regarded as the base of krystallos, though the exact formation is not fully explained.
items.cn: kryos「霜、严寒」一般认为是 krystallos 的词基；至于其确切构成方式，来源不确定，尚未完全解释清楚。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as crystallus (also crystallum), and it kept both the 'ice' and the 'clear quartz' senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这一希腊名词借入为 crystallus（亦作 crystallum），同时保留了「冰」与「透明石英」两义。

items.en: English crystal came through Latin and Old French in the fourteenth century, first for the mineral and soon after for clear glass.
items.cn: 英语 crystal 在十四世纪经拉丁语与古法语借入，先指这种矿物，不久又指透明玻璃。

items.en: From the seventeenth century crystal named lead glass, and in the twentieth century it was applied to quartz plates in radios and watches.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，crystal 指铅玻璃；到二十世纪，又被用于无线电与手表中的石英片。

items.en: Source generally regarded as established from Greek, but the derivation of krystallos from kryos is an accepted hypothesis rather than a proven step, and the earliest English use is only approximately dated.
items.cn: 来源一般认为可溯至希腊语；但 krystallos 由 kryos 派生属被接受的假说，其确切步骤为重构形式；最早的英语用例年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like crystal but come from other roots; group two holds materials and objects often called crystal.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的词；第二组是常被称为 crystal 的材料与物件。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of crystals' or 'clear like crystal'; it is a true relative, differing only in word class.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「晶体的」或「如水晶般清澈」的形容词；它是真正的同族词，只差词类。

entries.definition: The verb 'to form crystals' or 'to become definite'; it is derived from crystal, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「结晶」或「变得明确」的动词；它由 crystal 派生，并非形近词。

entries.definition: Means to baptize or name, from Christian, from Greek Christos 'anointed'; the resemblance is only in the first syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 意为施洗或命名，来自 Christian，源自希腊 Christos「受膏者」；相似只在前一音节。

entries.definition: A structure or substance that resembles a crystal, built with -oid 'like'; the ending differs from the noun crystal.
entries.definitionCN: 指类似晶体的结构或物质，后缀是 -oid「像」；词尾与名词 crystal 不同。

entries.definition: The mineral silicon dioxide; a crystal of quartz is one common kind of crystal, but crystal is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指二氧化硅矿物；石英晶体是晶体的一种常见类型，而 crystal 是总称。

entries.definition: A non-crystalline solid; crystal glass is a special clear glass, yet the two are chemically different in structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指非晶态固体；晶质玻璃是一种特殊透明玻璃，但两者在结构上不同。

entries.definition: A cut and polished stone valued for beauty; a crystal becomes a gem only after cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 指经切割抛光、以美观取胜的宝石；晶体只有切割后才成为宝石。

entries.definition: The regular arrangement of atoms inside a crystal; it names the structure, not the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指晶体内部原子的规则排列；它命名结构，而非物体本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek root, the real word family and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊词根、真实的词族与真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: Greek krystallos 'ice': clear quartz looked like ice that never melted.
normal.cn: 希腊 krystallos「冰」：透明石英看起来像永不融化的冰。

normal.en: The family runs crystal, crystalline, crystallize, crystallization, crystallography.
normal.cn: 词族包括 crystal、crystalline、crystallize、crystallization、crystallography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: crystal structure, single crystal, crystal growth, quartz crystal.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：晶体结构、单晶、晶体生长、石英晶体。

normal.en: Six flat faces and sharp edges are the visual signature of a well-grown crystal.
normal.cn: 六个平面与锐利棱边是长势良好的晶体的视觉标志。

normal.en: Everyday uses: sugar crystals, ice crystals, crystal glass, a crystal ball.
normal.cn: 日常用法：糖粒、冰晶、晶质玻璃、水晶球。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd standing in perfect rows without being told.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人不用口令就站成整齐的行列。

abstract.en: Picture light entering a room and leaving as a small rainbow.
abstract.cn: 想象光进入一间屋子，离开时变成一小段彩虹。

abstract.en: Picture time kept by a stone that vibrates instead of ticking.
abstract.cn: 想象时间由一块振动而非滴答作响的石头来计量。

examples.en: Each mineral species grows crystals with its own set of faces.
examples.cn: 每个矿物种长出的晶体都有自己的一套晶面。

examples.en: The wine glasses are lead crystal and ring when struck.
examples.cn: 这些酒杯是铅晶质玻璃，敲一下会发出清响。

examples.en: A quartz crystal regulates the frequency of the radio.
examples.cn: 一块石英晶体调节无线电的频率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克（cry）瑞士（stal）」——像瑞士冰峰一样透明坚硬的东西 → 晶体、水晶

root: 希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」，一般被认为源自 kryos「霜、严寒」；经拉丁 crystallus 与古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one object outward from its atomic order: the lattice, the natural specimen, the glass named after it, the objects made of that glass, the quartz inside a watch, the ice in a cloud, the ball of a fortune-teller, a grain of sugar and finally clearness itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项让同一物件从原子秩序向外展开：晶格、天然标本、以它命名的玻璃、由此制成的器物、表内的石英、云中的冰晶、占卜者的球、一粒糖，最后是清澈本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear six-sided column in which light breaks into points.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根透明六棱柱，光在里面碎成光点。

branches.en: ORDER AND SPECIMEN: the invisible lattice and the visible crystal are one thing seen two ways.
branches.cn: 秩序与标本：看不见的晶格与看得见的晶体，是同一事物的两种看法。

branches.en: GLASS NAMED AFTER STONE: lead glass borrowed the name and then lent it to bowls and chandeliers.
branches.cn: 以石命名的玻璃：铅玻璃借走这个名字，又把它借给碗与吊灯。

branches.en: TIME FROM STONE: a thin quartz plate keeps frequency steadier than any pendulum.
branches.cn: 以石计时：薄石英片比任何摆都更稳地维持频率。

branches.en: SMALL AND SYMBOLIC: an ice crystal is the same order at microscale, and a crystal ball turns it into a symbol of foresight.
branches.cn: 微小与象征：冰晶是同一秩序在微观尺度，水晶球则把它变成预见的象征。

branches.en: GRAIN AND CLARITY: the same word covers a grain of sugar and the transparency of a mountain lake.
branches.cn: 颗粒与清澈：同一个词既指一粒糖，也指山湖的透明。

intro.en: Crystal is a Greek loan whose root and derivatives are still transparent in English.
intro.cn: crystal 是希腊借词，其词根与派生词在英语中仍清晰可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus and crystallinus carried the Greek word into English; the Greek stem krystall- has no native Latin relative, so the entries are marked as Greek loans.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus 与 crystallinus 把希腊词带入英语；希腊词干 krystall- 在拉丁语中没有本土同族词，因此条目标注为希腊借词。

items.example: The Greek word named both ice and clear quartz.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词同时指冰与透明石英。

items.example: The crystal kept its six faces.
items.exampleCN: 这块晶体保留了六个晶面。

items.example: The salt crystallized on the rim.

items.exampleCN: 结晶提纯了这种化合物。

crystallum, crystali (n., second declension; Greek loan)

definition_zh: 结晶的；晶状的；晶体结构的；清澈如水晶的
definition_en: having the regular internal structure of a crystal, made of crystals, or clear like crystal
core_image: 冷库里，糖浆在勺背上结出一层细密糖粒，对着灯能看见规则的小平面
scene: 冷库里，糖浆慢慢冷却，勺背上结出一层细密的糖粒，对着灯能看见规则的小平面。The syrup cooled until a crystalline crust formed on the spoon.
sceneCN: 这里 crystalline 指「由晶体构成的、呈晶状的」（第 2 个义项：由晶体组成或具有晶质外观）；句意为糖浆冷却到勺背上结成一层晶状壳。可辨识物件：冷库、糖浆、勺背、细密糖粒、灯光下的小平面。

pos.zh: 结晶的；晶状的；晶体结构的；清澈的

senses.title: Having a regular crystal lattice
senses.definition: of a solid: having atoms arranged in a regular repeating lattice
senses.definitionCN: 指固体的原子按规则重复的晶格排列
senses.example: The syrup cooled until a crystalline crust formed on the spoon.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆冷却到勺背上结出一层晶状壳。
senses.why: -ine means 'of the nature of', so the adjective states lattice order rather than naming an object.
senses.whyCN: -ine 意为「具……性质的」，因此这个形容词陈述晶格秩序，而非命名物体。

senses.title: Made of or containing crystals
senses.definition: composed of visible crystals or grains
senses.definitionCN: 指由可见晶体或颗粒组成
senses.example: The vein is filled with crystalline calcite.
senses.exampleCN: 这条矿脉充填着晶质方解石。
senses.why: Visible grains are the hand-scale evidence of that order.
senses.whyCN: 可见颗粒是那种秩序在手边尺度上的证据。

senses.title: Of the crystalline state
senses.definition: of a physical state: ordered and solid, as opposed to glassy or amorphous
senses.definitionCN: 指有序的固态，与玻璃态或无定形态相对
senses.example: Cooling slowly keeps the metal in a crystalline state.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢冷却使金属保持结晶态。
senses.why: Physics contrasts the ordered state with the glassy one, and the adjective names the ordered side.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把有序态与玻璃态相对，这个形容词命名的是有序的一侧。

senses.title: Of a crystal material in technology
senses.definition: of materials such as silicon: made of one crystal or of many grains, as opposed to amorphous
senses.definitionCN: 指硅等材料由单晶或多晶构成，与无定形相对
senses.example: Crystalline silicon panels dominate the market.
senses.exampleCN: 晶体硅电池板在市场占主导。
senses.why: Industry turns the state into a product category, as in crystalline silicon.
senses.whyCN: 工业把这一状态变成产品类别，如晶体硅。

senses.title: Clear and transparent like crystal
senses.definition: literary: perfectly clear, as water, air or sound
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：如水、空气或声音般清澈
senses.example: A crystalline stream ran over the pebbles.
senses.exampleCN: 一条清澈的溪流漫过卵石。
senses.why: Transparency is the optical face of order, so clear water is called crystalline.
senses.whyCN: 透明是有序在光学上的面孔，因此清澈的水被称为 crystalline。

senses.title: Of the eye's lens
senses.definition: an anatomical use: the transparent lens of the eye
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学用法：眼球内透明的晶状体
senses.example: The surgeon replaced the crystalline lens.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生替换了晶状体。
senses.why: The eye's lens is a clear ordered body, and anatomy borrowed the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 眼的晶状体是透明而有序的物体，解剖学借用了这个形容词。

senses.title: Of rock with visible crystals
senses.definition: of rock: showing interlocking crystals rather than glass or fine mud
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石显示互相咬合的晶体，而非玻璃质或细泥质
senses.example: The crystalline rock sparkles in sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 这块结晶岩在阳光下闪亮。
senses.why: Rock that sparkles shows interlocking crystals rather than glass.
senses.whyCN: 闪光的岩石显示的是互相咬合的晶体，而非玻璃。

senses.title: Sharply clear in expression
senses.definition: figurative: of writing, logic or sound, unusually clear and precise
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：指文字、逻辑或声音异常清晰准确
senses.example: Her crystalline argument left no room for doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 她清晰锐利的论证不留疑问余地。
senses.why: Clarity of thought is the same quality transferred from matter to argument.
senses.whyCN: 思维的清晰是同一品质从物质转移到论证上。

intro.en: Crystalline is the Latin adjective built on crystallus, the Latin borrowing of Greek krystallos 'ice, rock crystal'.
intro.cn: crystalline 是建立在拉丁 crystallus 上的拉丁形容词，而 crystallus 是希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」的拉丁借词。

items.en: Krystallos named ice and clear quartz, the stone believed to be permanently frozen water.
items.cn: krystallos 指冰与透明石英，那种被认为永久冻结的水所成的石头。

items.en: Latin took the noun as crystallus and used it for both ice and the clear mineral.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个名词借为 crystallus，兼指冰与透明矿物。

items.en: The adjective crystallinus 'of crystal' was formed with -inus 'of the nature of', and it passed into English as crystalline.
items.cn: 形容词 crystallinus「水晶的」由 -inus「具……性质的」构成，进入英语成为 crystalline。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries crystalline was fixed as the opposite of amorphous, naming the ordered solid state.
items.cn: 在十八、十九世纪，crystalline 被固定为 amorphous 的反义词，命名有序的固态。

items.en: The same adjective named the eye's lens and, in literary writing, anything perfectly clear.
items.cn: 同一个形容词也用于眼的晶状体，并在文学写作中指任何极为清澈之物。

items.en: Source generally regarded as established through Greek, but the derivation of krystallos from kryos is an accepted hypothesis, and the exact date of the amorphous contrast is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源一般认为可溯至希腊语；但 krystallos 由 kryos 派生属被接受的假说，其确切步骤为重构形式；与 amorphous 对立的确切年代亦不确定。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives and nouns easily confused with crystalline; group two holds words for the same ordered state or its look.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 crystalline 混淆的形容词与名词；第二组是同一有序状态或其外观的词。

entries.definition: The object itself; crystalline is the adjective describing order or clarity.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体本身；crystalline 是描述有序或清澈的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb 'to form crystals'; it names the action that produces a crystalline solid.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「结晶」的动词；它命名产生结晶固体的动作。

entries.definition: A substance that resembles a crystal in some respects, built with -oid 'like' rather than -ine.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某些方面类似晶体的物质，后缀是 -oid「像」而非 -ine。

entries.definition: To baptize or name, from Christos 'anointed'; it shares only the opening sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指施洗或命名，来自 Christos「受膏者」；只共享开头读音。

entries.definition: Without regular internal order, as in glass; it is the standard opposite of crystalline.
entries.definitionCN: 指内部无规则秩序，如玻璃；它是 crystalline 的标准反义词。

entries.definition: Describes a solid that cooled too fast to order its atoms; it looks like glass rather than crystal.
entries.definitionCN: 指冷却太快、原子来不及排列的固体；它看起来像玻璃而非晶体。

entries.definition: Allows light through but not a clear image; crystalline water is clearer than translucent glass.
entries.definitionCN: 指透光但不能看清影像；crystalline 的水比半透明玻璃更清。

entries.definition: Made of many small crystals joined together, as most metals are; it is a subtype of crystalline.
entries.definitionCN: 指由许多小晶体结合而成，多数金属如此；它是 crystalline 的一个子类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin suffix, the real technical phrases and the real opposites.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁后缀、真实的技术搭配与真实的反义词。

normal.en: Crystal plus -ine: 'of the nature of a crystal', as in saline and serpentine.
normal.cn: crystal 加 -ine：「具晶体性质的」，如 saline 与 serpentine。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: crystalline structure, crystalline solid, crystalline rock, crystalline lens.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：晶体结构、结晶固体、结晶岩、晶状体。

normal.en: The technical opposite is amorphous, the state of glass.
normal.cn: 技术上的反义词是 amorphous，即玻璃态。

normal.en: The family runs crystal, crystalline, crystallize, crystallization, crystallinity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 crystal、crystalline、crystallize、crystallization、crystallinity。

normal.en: In electronics the contrast is crystalline silicon versus amorphous silicon.
normal.cn: 在电子学中，对比是晶体硅与无定形硅。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd that arranges itself into rows the moment it cools.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在冷却的一刻自动排成行列。

abstract.en: Picture a window that shows the view without blurring it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇不把景物弄糊的窗。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon coated in tiny mirrors after the syrup cools.
abstract.cn: 想象糖浆冷却后，勺背覆上一层小镜子。

examples.en: Slow cooling produces a coarse crystalline texture.
examples.cn: 缓慢冷却产生粗晶结构。

examples.en: Crystalline silicon is cut into thin wafers for solar cells.
examples.cn: 晶体硅被切成薄片用于太阳能电池。

examples.en: The lake was crystalline in the early morning light.
examples.cn: 清晨光里，湖面清澈如镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）来因（line）」——像水晶一样排得整齐的 → 结晶的

root: 拉丁 crystallus（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」借词）+ -inus「具……性质的」→ crystallinus，英语作 crystalline。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective from the invisible lattice to what the eye sees: the ordered solid, the visible grains, the state, the material, the clear water, the eye's lens, the sparkling rock and finally clear thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个形容词从看不见的晶格走到眼睛所见：有序固体、可见颗粒、结晶态、工业材料、清澈的水、眼的晶状体、闪亮的岩石，最后是清晰的思维。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sugar syrup cooling into a crust of tiny flat mirrors.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆冷却成一层由小镜面构成的壳。

branches.en: ORDER MADE VISIBLE: the lattice is invisible, and the grains show it at hand scale.
branches.cn: 秩序可见：晶格不可见，而颗粒在手的尺度上把它显示出来。

branches.en: STATE AND PRODUCT: the ordered state is the same whether in a cooled metal or a silicon wafer.
branches.cn: 状态与产品：无论冷却的金属还是硅片，有序状态相同。

branches.en: CLEAR WATER: transparency is the optical face of order.
branches.cn: 清澈的水：透明是有序在光学上的面孔。

branches.en: BODY AND ROCK: the eye's lens and a sparkling rock both show the same ordered solid.
branches.cn: 身体与岩石：眼的晶状体与闪亮的岩石都呈现同一种有序固体。

branches.en: CLEAR THOUGHT: clarity leaves matter and becomes a quality of argument.
branches.cn: 清晰思维：清澈离开物质，成为论证的品质。

intro.en: Crystalline is a Latin adjective whose suffix -ine also builds many English describing words.
intro.cn: crystalline 是拉丁形容词，其后缀 -ine 也构成许多英语描述词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus comes from Greek krystallos; -inus 'of the nature of' gives crystallinus, and English -ine continues that ending in saline, serpentine and crystalline.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus 来自希腊 krystallos；-inus「具……性质的」构成 crystallinus，英语 -ine 在 saline、serpentine、crystalline 中延续这一词尾。

items.example: The stem names the clear solid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名透明固体。

items.example: Saline means of the nature of salt.

latinEntries.structure: crystallus, crystalli (m., second declension; Greek loan)

definition_zh: 结晶；结晶作用；（计划、想法等的）具体化、明确成形
definition_en: the process by which crystals form from a solution or a melt, or the process by which an idea becomes definite
core_image: 糖厂车间里，浓缩糖浆在搅拌槽中冷却，槽壁上结出密密一层白色糖粒
scene: 糖厂车间里，浓缩的糖浆倒进搅拌槽，冷却后槽壁上结出密密的一层糖粒。Slow cooling and stirring promote crystallization of the sugar.
sceneCN: 这里 crystallization 指「溶质从溶液或熔体中析出、长成晶体的过程」（第 1 个义项：结晶作用）；句意为缓慢冷却与搅拌促进糖的结晶。可辨识物件：搅拌槽、浓缩糖浆、槽壁糖粒、冷却夹套。

senses.title: Formation of crystals from liquid
senses.titleCN: 从液体中长出晶体的过程
senses.definition: the process by which ordered crystals separate from a solution or a melt
senses.definitionCN: 指有序晶体从溶液或熔体中析出的过程
senses.example: Slow cooling and stirring promote crystallization of the sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢冷却与搅拌促进糖的结晶。
senses.why: -ation names the process, and the definition is the formation of ordered solid from liquid.
senses.whyCN: -ation 命名过程，定义即有序固体从液体中形成。

senses.title: Crystallization of magma
senses.definition: the geological process in which minerals crystallize from cooling magma
senses.definitionCN: 指矿物从冷却岩浆中结晶的地质过程
senses.example: Crystallization of the magma began with olivine.
senses.exampleCN: 岩浆的结晶从橄榄石开始。
senses.why: Magma is a melt, so its mineral growth is the geological case of the same process.
senses.whyCN: 岩浆是一种熔体，其矿物生长是同一过程的地质情形。

senses.title: Purification by crystallization
senses.definition: the use of repeated crystal formation to remove impurities from a substance
senses.definitionCN: 指反复结晶以除去杂质
senses.example: Repeated crystallization removed the last traces of salt.
senses.exampleCN: 反复结晶除去了最后一点盐。
senses.why: Repeated growth excludes impurities, which is what purification by crystallization means.
senses.whyCN: 反复生长排除杂质，这正是结晶提纯的含义。

senses.title: Controlled crystallization in industry
senses.definition: the controlled production of crystals of a chosen size in food or chemical plants
senses.definitionCN: 指在食品或化工厂中控制晶体尺寸的生产过程
senses.example: The factory controls crystallization to fix the grain size.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂控制结晶以固定晶粒尺寸。
senses.why: Industry controls temperature and stirring to fix grain size.
senses.whyCN: 工业控制温度与搅拌，以固定晶粒尺寸。

senses.title: Fractional crystallization
senses.definition: a separation method in which substances crystallize one after another as temperature falls
senses.definitionCN: 指随温度下降而使不同物质先后结晶的分离方法
senses.example: Fractional crystallization separated the two salts.
senses.exampleCN: 分步结晶把两种盐分离开。
senses.why: Different substances crystallize at different temperatures, which makes separation possible.
senses.whyCN: 不同物质在不同温度结晶，这才使分离成为可能。

senses.title: Ice crystallization
senses.definition: the formation of ice crystals in water, food or living tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指水、食品或活组织中冰晶的形成
senses.example: Ice crystallization cracked the water pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 冰的结晶把水管胀裂了。
senses.why: Water is a melt of ice, and its crystals form in cells and pipes.
senses.whyCN: 水是冰的熔体，其晶体在细胞与管道中形成。

senses.title: Becoming definite
senses.definition: the process by which plans, ideas or movements take a clear and fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、想法或运动取得清晰固定形态的过程
senses.example: The plan's crystallization took two years of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划用了两年谈判才成形。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an idea as a dissolved thing that becomes solid and definite.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把想法当作溶解之物，逐渐变硬、变明确。

senses.title: A concrete embodiment
senses.definition: the definite result in which an idea or tendency becomes visible and fixed
senses.definitionCN: 指使想法或趋势变得可见、固定的具体成果
senses.example: The treaty was the crystallization of a long rivalry.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约是长期对抗的具体结晶。
senses.why: The definite result is the embodiment, the last step of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 明确的结果就是具体化身，是同一意象的最后一步。

intro.en: Crystallization is crystal turned into a process noun by two Latin-descended suffixes, -ize and -ation.
intro.cn: crystallization 由 crystal 加两个拉丁来源后缀 -ize 与 -ation 构成过程名词。

items.en: Krystallos 'ice, rock crystal' passed through Latin crystallus into English crystal.
items.cn: krystallos「冰、水晶」经拉丁 crystallus 进入英语 crystal。

items.en: Latin -izare and Greek -izein formed verbs meaning 'to make, to become'; English -ize builds verbs such as crystallize.
items.cn: 拉丁 -izare 与希腊 -izein 构成表示「使……、成为……」的动词；英语 -ize 构成 crystallize 这类动词。

items.en: Latin -atio, -ationis names an action or process, so crystallization is the process, not one crystal.
items.cn: 拉丁 -atio、-ationis 命名动作或过程，因此 crystallization 指过程，而非某一颗晶体。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries the noun became standard in chemistry for purification and in geology for the growth of minerals from magma.
items.cn: 在十八、十九世纪，这个名词在化学中成为提纯的标准说法，在地质学中则指矿物从岩浆中生长。

items.en: Sugar refining gave the word a mass-production sense, and from the nineteenth century it was also used of ideas taking definite shape.
items.cn: 制糖业给这个词带来大批量生产的意义；从十九世纪起，它也被用于想法取得明确形态。

items.en: Not uncertain: the suffixal derivation is established. Only the first date of the figurative sense is approximate, and the Greek origin of krystallos is discussed under crystal.
items.cn: 并非存疑：后缀派生是确定的。仅比喻义的首次年代为约数，krystallos 的希腊来源见 crystal 词条。

note.en: Group one holds -ization words and family forms that look alike; group two holds the physical processes it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近的 -ization 词与同族形式；第二组是易与它混淆的物理过程。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -isation; it is the same word, not a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，用 -isation；是同一个词，不是另一过程。

entries.definition: The study and description of crystal structure, built with -graphy 'writing' rather than -ization 'process'.
entries.definitionCN: 指对晶体结构的研究与描述，后缀是 -graphy「书写」而非 -ization「过程」。

entries.definition: The medical burning of tissue, from Greek kautēr 'branding iron'; it shares the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 指医学上烧灼组织，来自希腊 kautēr「烙铁」；只共享词尾。

entries.definition: The degree to which a material is crystalline, an abstract property rather than an event.
entries.definitionCN: 指材料结晶的程度，是一种抽象属性而非事件。

entries.definition: The formation of a solid from a solution by reaction; crystallization is ordered growth, precipitation need not be ordered.
entries.definitionCN: 指反应使溶液析出固体；结晶是有序生长，沉淀则不必有序。

entries.definition: The general change from liquid to solid; crystallization is solidification that produces order.
entries.definitionCN: 指由液体变为固体的总过程；结晶是产生秩序的那种凝固。

entries.definition: The change from liquid to solid by cooling, usually of water; crystallization is the wider term.
entries.definitionCN: 指因冷却由液变固，通常指水；crystallization 是更宽的说法。

entries.definition: The formation of the first tiny crystal that later grows; it is the beginning of crystallization, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指后来会长大的第一个微晶形成；它是结晶的开端，不是全过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain and the real industrial and geological settings.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链与真实的工业、地质场景。

normal.en: Crystal, crystallize, crystallization: the noun of the process, built by -ize and -ation.
normal.cn: crystal、crystallize、crystallization：由 -ize 与 -ation 构成的过程名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fractional crystallization, crystallization temperature, water of crystallization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：分步结晶、结晶温度、结晶水。

normal.en: In a solution, cooling and stirring bring the first nuclei and then growth.
normal.cn: 在溶液里，降温与搅拌先带来晶核，然后是长大。

normal.en: In geology the sequence is olivine, pyroxene, feldspar, quartz, the Bowen series.
normal.cn: 在地质学中顺序是橄榄石、辉石、长石、石英，即鲍文反应系列。

normal.en: The figurative use says a plan crystallizes when it stops being vague.
normal.cn: 比喻用法说计划「结晶」，意思是它不再模糊。

abstract.en: Picture a cloud of dissolved salt deciding where to put its first solid corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一团溶解的盐决定把第一个固体角落放在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture an idea slowly hardening into a building you can walk into.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法慢慢硬化成一栋可以走进去的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture winter turning a puddle into a floor of tiny panes.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天把水洼变成一层小玻璃板。

examples.en: Fractional crystallization is used to separate salts with different solubilities.
examples.cn: 分步结晶用于分离溶解度不同的盐。

examples.en: The crystallization of magma releases latent heat into the surrounding rock.
examples.cn: 岩浆结晶把潜热释放到周围岩石中。

examples.en: Water of crystallization is lost when the blue crystals are heated.
examples.cn: 加热蓝色晶体时，结晶水会失去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）里（li）扎（za）tion」——晶粒一颗颗扎堆长出来 → 结晶

root: crystal（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」）+ -ize（拉丁 -izare / 希腊 -izein，使……）+ -ation（拉丁 -atio，动作名词后缀）→ crystallization「结晶过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process from solution to symbol: crystals nucleate and grow, then do it underground, in a refinery, in a plant, in a separation column, in ice, in a plan and finally in a treaty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程从溶液走到象征：晶体成核并长大，然后依次发生在地下、精炼厂、工厂、分离柱、冰里、计划里，最后在条约里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tank wall slowly furred with white grains as the syrup cools.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆冷却时，槽壁慢慢结满白色颗粒。

branches.en: FROM LIQUID TO ORDER: water and syrup follow the same nucleation-and-growth path.
branches.cn: 从液体到秩序：水与糖浆走同一条成核—生长路径。

branches.en: UNDERGROUND: magma crystallizes minerals in a fixed sequence as it cools.
branches.cn: 地下：岩浆冷却时按固定顺序结晶出矿物。

branches.en: PURITY AND PRODUCT: repeated growth removes impurities, and controlled growth fixes grain size.
branches.cn: 纯度与产品：反复生长除去杂质，受控生长固定晶粒尺寸。

branches.en: SEPARATION: falling temperature makes different substances crystallize one by one.
branches.cn: 分离：降温使不同物质先后结晶。

branches.en: THE IDEA TAKES SHAPE: what was vague becomes a plan, and then a document.
branches.cn: 想法成形：模糊之物先成为计划，再成为文件。

intro.en: Crystallization stacks a Greek noun with two derivational suffixes, so the whole word reads as 'the process of making crystal'.
intro.cn: crystallization 把一个希腊名词与两个派生后缀叠起来，整词读作「使成晶体的过程」。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus (from Greek krystallos) supplies the base; -izare and -atio supply the verb and the process noun, as in organized and organization.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus（源自希腊 krystallos）提供词基；-izare 与 -atio 提供动词与过程名词，如 organized 与 organization。

items.example: The stem names the ordered solid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名有序固体。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成动词。

items.example: The sugar crystallized on the wall.
Organization is the act of organizing.

items.meaning: a vessel in which crystals form

latinEntries.structure: crystallus, crystalli (m., second declension; Greek loan)

definition_zh: 结晶；使结晶；（想法、计划）变得明确；裹糖（糖渍）
definition_en: to form crystals or cause something to form crystals; to become or make something clear and definite
core_image: 作坊里，裹了糖的姜片摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒
scene: 作坊里，师傅把煮好的姜片裹上糖，摊在竹筛上晾干，糖层慢慢结成白色颗粒。The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
sceneCN: 这里 crystallize 指「（糖浆在表面）结晶、形成糖霜」（第 5 个义项：用糖包裹并使其结晶，即糖渍）；句意为糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。可辨识物件：竹筛、糖渍姜片、白色糖霜、冷却的糖浆。

senses.title: Form crystals (intransitive)
senses.definition: of a substance: to separate from a liquid as ordered solid crystals
senses.definitionCN: 指物质从液体中析出为有序固体晶体
senses.example: The ginger slices crystallize as the sugar syrup cools around them.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆在姜片周围冷却时，姜片逐渐结晶挂霜。
senses.why: The intransitive use describes the substance acting on its own.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法描述物质自身发生的变化。

senses.title: Cause crystals to form
senses.definition: to make a dissolved substance form crystals, as by cooling or seeding
senses.definitionCN: 指通过降温或加晶种使溶解物形成晶体
senses.example: Chemists crystallize the compound by cooling its saturated solution.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家通过冷却饱和溶液使化合物结晶。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent who cools or seeds the solution.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加一个降温或加晶种的施事。

senses.title: Become definite
senses.definition: of plans or ideas: to take a clear and fixed form after being vague
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或想法从模糊变得清晰固定
senses.example: Their vague proposal crystallized into a detailed scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 他们含糊的提议具体成了一项详细方案。
senses.why: Plans become definite the way crystals become solid.
senses.whyCN: 计划变明确，正如晶体变固体。

senses.title: Make something definite
senses.definition: to give a clear and fixed form to an idea, plan or movement
senses.definitionCN: 指使想法、计划或运动取得清晰固定的形态
senses.example: The speech crystallized the demands of the movement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇演说把这场运动的要求明确固定下来。
senses.why: An agent can make an idea definite, matching the transitive pattern.
senses.whyCN: 施事可以使想法变明确，与及物模式相合。

senses.title: Coat and preserve with sugar
senses.definition: to coat fruit or peel with sugar syrup that then crystallizes
senses.definitionCN: 指用糖浆包裹水果或果皮，并使糖层结晶
senses.example: They crystallize orange peel for the holiday market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们糖渍橙皮供应节日市场。
senses.why: Sugar coating is literal crystallization on a fruit's surface.
senses.whyCN: 裹糖就是字面意义上的结晶发生在果皮表面。

senses.title: Freeze into ice crystals
senses.definition: of water: to turn into ice crystals, especially in food or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 指水结成冰晶，尤指在食品或组织中
senses.example: Water crystallizes in the cells and bursts them.
senses.exampleCN: 水在细胞里结晶，把细胞胀破。
senses.why: Water in cells crystallizes and expands, which is why it bursts them.
senses.whyCN: 细胞里的水结晶并膨胀，这正是它胀破细胞的原因。

senses.title: Separate out as crystals
senses.definition: to come out of a solution as solid crystals, often with 'out'
senses.definitionCN: 指从溶液中以固体晶体形式析出，常与 out 连用
senses.example: The salt crystallized out as the water evaporated.
senses.exampleCN: 水蒸发时盐结晶析出。
senses.why: The particle out marks separation from solution.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 out 标记从溶液中分离出来。

senses.title: Develop into a clear form
senses.definition: to develop into a recognizable and organized form, often with 'into'
senses.definitionCN: 指发展成可辨识、有组织的形态，常与 into 连用
senses.example: The protest crystallized into a national campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议发展成一场全国性运动。
senses.why: The particle into marks development into a recognized form.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 into 标记发展为可辨识的形态。

intro.en: Crystallize is an English verb coined on crystal with the Latin-derived suffix -ize, following the pattern of French and Latin verbs in -iser and -izare.
intro.cn: crystallize 是在 crystal 上加拉丁来源后缀 -ize 构成的英语动词，仿照法语 -iser 与拉丁 -izare 的动词模式。

items.en: Krystallos 'ice, rock crystal' gave Latin crystallus and English crystal.
items.cn: krystallos「冰、水晶」产生拉丁 crystallus 与英语 crystal。

items.en: Latin -izare, from Greek -izein, formed verbs meaning 'to make or become'; it entered English through French -iser.
items.cn: 拉丁 -izare（源自希腊 -izein）构成表示「使……、成为……」的动词，经法语 -iser 进入英语。

items.en: The verb appears in seventeenth-century chemical writing for the formation of salt crystals from solution.
items.cn: 这个动词在十七世纪化学文献中出现，指盐从溶液中形成晶体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the verb to minerals forming from cooling magma and to ice forming in rock cracks.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学把这个动词用于矿物从冷却岩浆中形成，以及岩石裂隙中冰的形成。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries crystallize became a common figure for ideas and movements taking definite shape.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，crystallize 成为想法与运动取得明确形态的常用比喻。

items.en: Not uncertain: the formation from crystal plus -ize is transparent. Only the exact first date of the figurative use is approximate.
items.cn: 并非存疑：由 crystal 加 -ize 构成这一点清楚可读。仅比喻义的准确首次年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like crystallize but differ in root or spelling; group two holds verbs for becoming solid or definite.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根或拼写不同的动词；第二组是表示变硬或变明确的动词。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -ise; it is the same verb, not a different process.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写，用 -ise；是同一个动词，不是另一过程。

entries.definition: To burn tissue to stop bleeding, from Greek kautēr 'branding iron'; it shares the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 指烧灼组织以止血，来自希腊 kautēr「烙铁」；只共享词尾。

entries.definition: The noun from which the verb is formed; it names the object that results, not the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该动词的名词；它命名产生的结果对象，而非产生它的动作。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective, as in crystallized fruit; it names the result, not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词兼形容词，如糖渍水果；它命名结果而非动作。

entries.definition: The general verb for turning liquid into solid; crystallize adds the idea of ordered growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指液体变固体的总称；crystallize 增加有序生长之意。

entries.definition: To come out of a solution as a solid, often without crystal order; a chemical rather than a structural emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 指从溶液中析出固体，常无晶体秩序；强调化学而非结构。

entries.definition: To become hard or firm, without saying anything about internal order.
entries.definitionCN: 指变硬变坚，不涉及内部秩序。

entries.definition: An idiom for a plan or idea becoming definite; crystallize is its more formal single-word equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指计划或想法变明确的口语说法；crystallize 是更正式的单词对应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real phrasal verbs and the real confectionery use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的短语动词与真实的糖渍用法。

normal.en: Crystal plus -ize: to make or become crystal, exactly as the suffix says.
normal.cn: crystal 加 -ize：使成晶体或成为晶体，正如后缀所示。

normal.en: Two phrasal verbs carry much of the meaning: crystallize out and crystallize into.
normal.cn: 两个短语动词承载了大部分词义：结晶析出与具体形成为。

normal.en: The family runs crystal, crystalline, crystallize, crystallization, crystallized.
normal.cn: 词族包括 crystal、crystalline、crystallize、crystallization、crystallized。

normal.en: In the kitchen the verb means candied: crystallized ginger, crystallized peel.
normal.cn: 在厨房里这个动词指糖渍：糖姜片、糖橙皮。

normal.en: In writing it means making an idea sharp: a speech crystallizes demands.
normal.cn: 在写作中它指使想法锐利：一篇演说把要求明确下来。

abstract.en: Picture a fog that suddenly knows what shape it wants to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾突然知道自己想成为什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture an argument freezing into a single clear sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一场争论冻结成一句清楚的话。

abstract.en: Picture sugar putting on armour one grain at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象糖一粒一粒地穿上盔甲。

examples.en: Salt crystallizes out when the brine is concentrated.
examples.cn: 盐水浓缩时盐结晶析出。

examples.en: The movement crystallized into a political party within a year.
examples.cn: 这场运动在一年内发展成一个政党。

examples.en: Crystallized ginger is sold in small paper bags.
examples.cn: 糖姜片装在小纸袋里出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克瑞斯（crystal）来（li）z」——让东西像水晶那样定形 → 结晶、明确

root: crystal（希腊 krystallos「冰、水晶」）+ -ize（拉丁 -izare，源自希腊 -izein，使……、成为……）→ crystallize「使结晶；使明确」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb in two directions: matter forms crystals, and ideas form shapes, with sugar, ice, solutions and movements each taking part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词朝两个方向展开：物质结成晶体，想法结成形体，糖、冰、溶液与运动各自参与其中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: syrup drying into a hard white coat on a slice of ginger.
core.cn: 核心意象：糖浆在姜片上晾成一层硬白霜。

branches.en: MAKE AND BECOME: the verb works both without and with an object.
branches.cn: 使然与自然：这个动词既可不及物，也可及物。

branches.en: THE IDEA SETS: vague proposals harden into schemes and demands.
branches.cn: 想法定形：含糊的提议硬化为方案与要求。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND ICE: sugar and water both crystallize on a surface or in a cell.
branches.cn: 厨房与冰：糖与水都会在表面或细胞内结晶。

branches.en: OUT OF SOLUTION: the technical phrasal verb for material leaving a liquid as solid.
branches.cn: 从溶液中析出：物质以固体离开液体的技术短语。

branches.en: INTO A FORM: a movement develops a recognizable body.
branches.cn: 成为形态：一场运动发展出可辨识的躯体。

intro.en: Crystallize is a noun plus a verb-forming suffix, and the suffix is shared with hundreds of English verbs.
intro.cn: crystallize 是名词加动词后缀，这个后缀与数百个英语动词共享。

latinIntro.en: Latin crystallus gives the base; -izare, from Greek -izein, gives the verb pattern seen in organize, realize and crystallize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crystallus 提供词基；-izare（源自希腊 -izein）提供 organize、realize、crystallize 中的动词模式。

items.example: The stem names the ordered solid.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名有序固体。

items.example: Organize means to make an organization.

items.meaning: having formed crystals; coated with sugar
in the process of forming crystals

items.example: Crystallization began at the cooler wall.
items.exampleCN: 结晶从较冷的槽壁开始。

latinEntries.structure: crystallus, crystalli (m., second declension; Greek loan)

definition_zh: 侵蚀；腐蚀；削弱；逐渐丧失
definition_en: the wearing away of rock or soil by water, wind or ice, or the gradual weakening and loss of something abstract
core_image: 河谷里，河水年复一年磨掉崖脚，岸边泥土不断塌落，崖顶的草皮向后退
scene: 河谷里，河水年复一年磨掉崖脚，岸边的泥土不断塌落。River erosion has cut the gorge deeper each century.
sceneCN: 这里 erosion 指「水流、风或冰对岩石与土壤的磨蚀搬移」（第 1 个义项：自然营力造成的侵蚀）；句意为河流侵蚀使峡谷每个世纪都更深一些。可辨识物件：河谷、崖脚、塌落的泥土、崖顶草皮。

pos.zh: 侵蚀；腐蚀；削弱；逐渐丧失

senses.title: Wearing away by natural forces
senses.definition: the process by which water, wind, ice or waves wear away rock and soil
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风、冰或浪磨蚀岩石与土壤的过程
senses.example: River erosion has cut the gorge deeper each century.
senses.exampleCN: 河流侵蚀使峡谷每个世纪都更深一些。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'gnaw out', and geology applied it to the slow removal of land.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「啃出去」，地质学把它用于陆地的缓慢移除。

senses.title: The worn result or feature
senses.titleCN: 侵蚀造成的结果或地形
senses.definition: the worn surface, shape or feature left after material has been removed
senses.definitionCN: 指物质被移除后留下的磨蚀面、形状或地形
senses.example: The arch is a famous product of erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座拱门是侵蚀的著名产物。
senses.why: The worn shape is the visible remainder of the process.
senses.whyCN: 被磨出的形状是这一过程留下的可见残余。

senses.title: Loss of soil
senses.definition: the removal of topsoil by water or wind, usually as an agricultural problem
senses.definitionCN: 指水或风带走表土，通常作为农业问题
senses.example: Terracing reduced soil erosion on the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 梯田减少了坡地上的土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Topsoil is the most valuable layer removed, so agriculture gave the process its own phrase.
senses.whyCN: 表土是被移除的最有价值的一层，农业因此给了这一过程一个专门说法。

senses.title: Coastal and beach loss
senses.definition: the retreat of a coastline or beach under wave action
senses.definitionCN: 指海岸线或海滩在波浪作用下后退
senses.example: Coastal erosion threatens the row of houses.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸侵蚀威胁着那排房屋。
senses.why: Waves are the agent at the coast, and the retreat is the measurable result.
senses.whyCN: 波浪是海岸上的营力，后退是可测的结果。

senses.title: Gradual loss of value or profit
senses.titleCN: 价值或利润的逐渐流失
senses.definition: the slow reduction of money, profit or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 指金钱、利润或优势缓慢减少
senses.example: Price competition caused a steady erosion of margins.
senses.exampleCN: 价格竞争造成利润率的持续侵蚀。
senses.why: Money is removed the way rock is: slowly, by contact, and never all at once.
senses.whyCN: 金钱像岩石一样被移除：缓慢、靠接触，且从不会一次全没。

senses.title: Weakening of rights or trust
senses.definition: the gradual weakening of rights, trust or standards
senses.definitionCN: 指权利、信任或准则逐渐削弱
senses.example: The new rules led to an erosion of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定导致隐私受到侵蚀。
senses.why: Rights are removed by small steps rather than one blow, which is why erosion fits.
senses.whyCN: 权利是靠小步而非一击被移除，这正是「侵蚀」贴合的原因。

senses.title: Dental erosion
senses.definition: the chemical wearing away of tooth enamel by acid
senses.definitionCN: 指酸对牙釉质的化学性磨损
senses.example: Fizzy drinks contribute to dental erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 碳酸饮料会加剧牙齿酸蚀。
senses.why: Acid removes enamel chemically, and dentistry borrowed the geological word.
senses.whyCN: 酸以化学方式移除牙釉质，牙科借用了这个地质词。

senses.title: Decline of support or membership
senses.definition: the gradual loss of supporters, members or political base
senses.definitionCN: 指支持者、成员或政治基础的逐渐流失
senses.example: The party suffered erosion of its rural base.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在农村的基础遭到侵蚀。
senses.why: Support drains away gradually, like a coast retreating.
senses.whyCN: 支持逐渐流失，就像海岸后退。

intro.en: Erosion is a Latin noun of action from erodere 'to gnaw out', built from a prefix of removal and a verb for gnawing.
intro.cn: erosion 是拉丁动词 erodere「咬出、啃去」的动作名词，由表示移除的前缀与「啃咬」动词构成。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw, nibble, wear by gnawing' supplied the root; its own deeper origin is uncertain, and comparisons with Sanskrit rad- 'scratch' are hypotheses.
items.cn: rodere「啃、咬、啮磨」提供词根；它更深的来源不确定，与梵语 rad-「刮」的比较只是假说。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere produced erodere 'to gnaw away, eat out', used of animals and of acids long before geology.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere「啃掉、蚀出」，在地质学之前很久就用于动物与酸。

items.en: Erosio, erosionis 'a gnawing away' is the action noun; English took it through French erosion in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: erosio、erosionis「啃蚀」是动作名词；英语在十六世纪经法语 erosion 借入。

items.en: Early English uses were medical and chemical, describing ulcers and the action of acids on metals.
items.cn: 早期英语用法属医学与化学，描写溃疡以及酸对金属的作用。

items.en: From the eighteenth century erosion became the standard geological term for the wearing away of land by water, wind and ice.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，erosion 成为标准地质术语，指水、风、冰对陆地的磨蚀。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of rodere is unsettled, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the noun's own Latin derivation is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：rodere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式；该名词本身的拉丁派生是确定的。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble erosion in sound or spelling; group two holds processes of wearing away and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组是读音或拼写近似 erosion 的词；第二组是磨蚀过程及其反义词。

entries.definition: The act of avoiding or escaping, from e- 'out' plus vadere 'go'; the ending matches, the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指逃避或躲开，来自 e-「出」加 vadere「走」；词尾相合，词根不同。

entries.definition: A volcanic or sudden outburst, from e- plus rumpere 'break'; geologists keep it separate from erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 指火山喷发或突然爆发，来自 e- 加 rumpere「破裂」；地质学把它与侵蚀分开。

entries.definition: A rare medical word for scraping away tissue, from eradere 'to scrape out', a relative through the same rodere root.
entries.definitionCN: 指刮除组织的罕见医学词，来自 eradere「刮出」，经同一 rodere 词根与之相关。

entries.definition: Means able to be eroded, built with -ible; it shares the root but describes susceptibility rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为易受侵蚀的，由 -ible 构成；共享词根，但描述易受性而非过程。

entries.definition: Wearing by friction, as sand rubbing a surface; erosion includes removal by transport as well as rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦造成的磨损，如砂磨表面；erosion 除摩擦外还包括搬运移除。

entries.definition: The breakdown of rock where it lies, without removal; erosion then carries the pieces away.
entries.definitionCN: 指岩石在原地崩解而未被搬走；erosion 再把碎块带走。

entries.definition: Chemical wearing of metal or rock, especially by acid; it is a chemical cousin of erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 指金属或岩石受化学作用磨损，尤指酸蚀；它是 erosion 的化学近亲。

entries.definition: The laying down of material; it is the counterpart of erosion in the sediment budget.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质的堆积；在沉积收支中与侵蚀相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real word family and the real policy and dental phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的词族与真实的政策、牙科搭配。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus rodere 'gnaw': erosion is gnawing something out of the land.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rodere「啃」：侵蚀就是把东西从地里啃出去。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible, erosivity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible、erosivity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: soil erosion, coastal erosion, erosion rate, erosion control.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：土壤侵蚀、海岸侵蚀、侵蚀速率、侵蚀防治。

normal.en: Weathering breaks rock in place, erosion carries it away.
normal.cn: 风化在原地弄碎岩石，侵蚀把它搬走。

normal.en: The abstract use is regular: erosion of confidence, of margins, of privacy.
normal.cn: 抽象用法很规律：信心、利润率、隐私的侵蚀。

abstract.en: Picture a cliff that loses one grain for every wave and never notices.
abstract.cn: 想象一处崖壁每道浪带走一粒沙，却从不察觉。

abstract.en: Picture a savings account quietly eaten by fees.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被手续费悄悄吃掉的储蓄账户。

abstract.en: Picture a right that disappears not by law but by habit.
abstract.cn: 想象一项权利不是被法律取消，而是被习惯磨掉。

examples.en: Wind erosion stripped the field down to bare subsoil.
examples.cn: 风蚀把田地剥到只剩生土。

examples.en: Erosion of confidence followed the second product failure.
examples.cn: 第二次产品失败之后，信心受到侵蚀。

examples.en: Dentists warn that sweet drinks speed up enamel erosion.
examples.cn: 牙医警告甜饮料会加速牙釉质酸蚀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一（e）揉（ro）神（sion）」——被水一遍遍揉掉 → 侵蚀

root: 拉丁 e-「出」+ rodere「啃、啮」→ erodere「啃掉」；再加 -io（动作名词后缀）→ erosio「啃蚀」，英语作 erosion。rodere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loss: a force removes material, and the same slow removal then appears as a landform, as lost soil, as a retreating coast, as shrinking profit, as weakened rights, as worn enamel and as a vanishing base.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种失去展开：某种力量带走物质，同一种缓慢移除随后表现为地形、流失的表土、后退的海岸、缩水的利润、被削弱的权利、磨薄的牙釉质与消散的基础。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river grinding the foot of a cliff while the grass above edges backward.
core.cn: 核心意象：河水磨掉崖脚，上方的草皮向后退。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: the wearing and the worn shape are two views of one event.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：磨蚀与磨出的形状是同一事件的两种看法。

branches.en: TWO SCENES: a ploughed slope and a storm beach lose ground in the same way.
branches.cn: 两个场景：耕地坡面与风暴海滩以同样方式失去土地。

branches.en: MONEY WEARS: margins shrink the way cliffs do, slowly and irreversibly.
branches.cn: 金钱也会磨蚀：利润率像崖壁一样缓慢且不可逆地缩小。

branches.en: RIGHTS WEAR: what is not defended is quietly removed.
branches.cn: 权利也会磨蚀：无人守护的东西被悄悄移除。

branches.en: BODY AND BODY POLITIC: acid eats enamel, and indifference eats a party's base.
branches.cn: 身体与政治体：酸啃牙釉质，冷漠啃掉政党基础。

intro.en: Erosion is a Latin action noun whose prefix, root and suffix each recur in English.
intro.cn: erosion 是拉丁动作名词，其前缀、词根与后缀都在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin rodere 'to gnaw' gives erode, erosion, corrode and rodent; e- 'out' marks removal, and -io marks the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rodere「啃」衍生 erode、erosion、corrode 与 rodent；e-「出」标记移除，-io 标记动作。

items.exampleCN: 降雨侵蚀力随季节变化。

items.meaning: to eat away by chemical action

definition_zh: 侵蚀；磨蚀；逐渐削弱；使逐渐丧失
definition_en: to wear away rock or soil gradually, or to weaken and reduce something such as value, trust or rights
core_image: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软岩层一点点掏空，崖顶草地不断向后退
scene: 海浪日夜拍打崖壁，把松软的岩层一点点掏空，崖顶的草地正往后退。Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
sceneCN: 这里 erode 指「（自然营力）逐渐磨掉、掏空岩体」（第 1 个义项：侵蚀岩石或土壤）；句意为海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。可辨识物件：崖壁、浪花、掏空的岩层、崖顶草地。

senses.title: Wear away rock or soil
senses.definition: of water, wind or ice: to wear away rock or soil gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指水、风或冰逐渐磨掉岩石或土壤
senses.example: Waves erode the soft cliff a little more each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 海浪每个冬天都多啃掉一点这段软崖。
senses.why: The transitive verb puts the agent first: waves erode cliffs.
senses.whyCN: 及物动词把营力放在前面：波浪侵蚀崖壁。

senses.title: Be worn away
senses.definition: to be worn away gradually by natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 指受自然营力逐渐磨蚀
senses.example: The old shore erodes faster than the headland.
senses.exampleCN: 旧岸比岬角侵蚀得更快。
senses.why: The intransitive verb lets the surface itself be the subject.
senses.whyCN: 不及物动词让表面本身成为主语。

senses.title: Reduce value or profit
senses.definition: to reduce money, profit or advantage gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指逐渐减少金钱、利润或优势
senses.example: Freight costs erode the profit on each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 运费侵蚀着每箱货的利润。
senses.why: Costs remove profit as water removes rock.
senses.whyCN: 成本移除利润，正如水移除岩石。

senses.title: Weaken confidence or trust
senses.definition: to make confidence, trust or reputation gradually weaker
senses.definitionCN: 指使信心、信任或声誉逐渐减弱
senses.example: Repeated delays eroded public trust in the project.
senses.exampleCN: 一再延误削弱了公众对这个项目的信任。
senses.why: Repeated failure removes trust grain by grain.
senses.whyCN: 反复失败一粒一粒地移除信任。

senses.title: Wear down rights or standards
senses.definition: to weaken rights, freedoms or standards by small steps
senses.definitionCN: 指以渐进方式削弱权利、自由或准则
senses.example: Emergency powers eroded the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 紧急权力侵蚀了集会权。
senses.why: Small legal steps remove rights the way waves remove a cliff.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的小步移除权利，正如波浪移除崖壁。

senses.title: Wear away chemically
senses.definition: of acid: to eat into a surface such as enamel or metal
senses.definitionCN: 指酸对牙釉质、金属等表面的侵蚀
senses.example: Stomach acid can erode tooth enamel.
senses.exampleCN: 胃酸会侵蚀牙釉质。
senses.why: Acid attacks enamel at the chemical scale.
senses.whyCN: 酸在化学尺度上攻击牙釉质。

senses.title: Cut into the land
senses.definition: of a river: to cut a channel or valley into the land
senses.definitionCN: 指河流在地表切出河道或河谷
senses.example: The river erodes a narrow gorge through the limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在石灰岩中切出一条窄峡谷。
senses.why: A river removes bed and bank, which is how it cuts a channel.
senses.whyCN: 河流移除河床与河岸，正是这样切出河道。

senses.title: Gradually weaken an advantage or base
senses.definition: to reduce an advantage, majority or base by small degrees
senses.definitionCN: 指逐步减少优势、多数席位或基础
senses.example: New competitors eroded the firm's lead.
senses.exampleCN: 新的竞争者削弱了这家公司的领先地位。
senses.why: Competition removes a lead by small degrees.
senses.whyCN: 竞争一点一点地移除领先优势。

intro.en: Erode comes from Latin erodere 'to gnaw out', the same verb that stands behind erosion.
intro.cn: erode 来自拉丁 erodere「啃出、蚀去」，与 erosion 出自同一动词。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' is the root verb; its pre-Latin origin is not established, and suggested Indo-European links are hypotheses.
items.cn: rodere「啃」是词根动词；它在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，所提出的印欧关联均属假说。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere gave erodere 'to gnaw away, eat into', used of animals, acids and ulcers before it was used of land.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere「啃掉、蚀入」，在用于土地之前，先用于动物、酸与溃疡。

items.en: English took the verb from French eroder or directly from Latin in the seventeenth century, at first in medical and chemical contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经法语 eroder 或直接自拉丁语借入该动词，最初用于医学与化学语境。

items.en: In the nineteenth century erode became the everyday geological verb paired with erosion, and it was applied to rivers, glaciers and waves.
items.cn: 在十九世纪，erode 成为与 erosion 配对的地质日常动词，用于河流、冰川与波浪。

items.en: From the twentieth century the verb spread to money, trust and rights, where the image of slow removal still governs the meaning.
items.cn: 从二十世纪起，这个动词扩展到金钱、信任与权利，其中「缓慢移除」的形象仍主导词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the deeper origin of rodere is unsettled. The route from Latin erodere to English erode is established, though the exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：rodere 的更深来源没有定论。从拉丁 erodere 到英语 erode 的路径是确定的，但确切首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that look like erode but have other roots; group two holds verbs of wearing away and weakening.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的动词；第二组是表示磨损与削弱的动词。

entries.definition: To escape or avoid, from e- 'out' plus vadere 'go'; it shares the prefix and the sound but not the 'gnaw' root.
entries.definitionCN: 指逃脱或避开，来自 e-「出」加 vadere「走」；共享前缀与读音，但没有「啃」的词根。

entries.definition: To burst out, from e- plus rumpere 'break'; volcanic eruptions are the opposite of slow wearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指爆发，来自 e- 加 rumpere「破裂」；火山喷发与缓慢磨蚀正相反。

entries.definition: To eat away chemically, from cor- 'thoroughly' plus rodere; it is a true relative that stresses chemical attack.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学性蚀去，来自 cor-「彻底」加 rodere；它是真正的同族词，强调化学侵蚀。

entries.definition: To rub out or delete, from eradere 'to scrape out', built on the same rodere root; it means removing marks, not wearing land.
entries.definitionCN: 指擦掉或删除，来自 eradere「刮出」，建立在同一 rodere 词根上；它指去除痕迹，而非磨蚀土地。

entries.definition: The everyday equivalent for slow removal by friction or weather; erode is its technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或风化造成缓慢移除的日常说法；erode 是其技术对应词。

entries.definition: To rub or scrape a surface, from ab- 'away' plus radere 'scrape'; it stresses contact friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指摩擦或刮削表面，来自 ab-「离开」加 radere「刮」；强调接触摩擦。

entries.definition: To carry off by water, as soil from a field; erode is the geological term for the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 指被水冲走，如田里的土；erode 是同一动作的地质术语。

entries.definition: To weaken something gradually, often secretly, from under- plus mine; it is the figurative cousin of erode.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐、常为暗中地削弱，来自 under- 加 mine；它是 erode 的比喻近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real verb family and the real abstract collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的动词词族与真实的抽象搭配。

normal.en: E- 'out' plus rodere 'gnaw': to gnaw material out of a surface.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rodere「啃」：把材料从表面啃出去。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible, erosivity.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible、erosivity。

normal.en: The same root appears in corrode, erase and rodent.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 corrode、erase 与 rodent 中。

normal.en: Fixed abstract phrases: erode confidence, erode trust, erode margins, erode rights.
normal.cn: 固定抽象搭配：削弱信心、侵蚀信任、侵蚀利润、侵蚀权利。

normal.en: In landscape writing erode takes a direct object: rivers erode valleys, waves erode cliffs.
normal.cn: 在地貌写作中 erode 直接带宾语：河流侵蚀河谷，海浪侵蚀崖壁。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step is a little lower than last year.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，每一级都比去年低一点。

abstract.en: Picture a promise rubbed thin by being repeated too often.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺因反复重申而被磨薄。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that never breaks anything, only carries one grain away.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪从不打碎什么，只带走一粒沙。

examples.en: The river has eroded a channel thirty metres deep.
examples.cn: 这条河已切出三十米深的河道。

examples.en: Rising costs eroded the profit margin on the product.
examples.cn: 成本上升侵蚀了该产品的利润率。

examples.en: Repeated scandals eroded voters' trust in the council.
examples.cn: 接连的丑闻削弱了选民对议会的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一（e）揉的（rode）」——被水一揉就掉 → 侵蚀

root: 拉丁 e-「出」+ rodere「啃、啮」→ erodere「啃掉、蚀去」；英语经法语 eroder 或直接自拉丁语借入。rodere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb from the cliff to the balance sheet: a force removes material, then the same slow removal appears as a channel, as lost profit, as weakened trust, as narrowed rights, as etched enamel and as a shrinking lead.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个动词从崖壁走到账本：某种力量带走物质，同一种缓慢移除随后表现为河道、流失的利润、被削弱的信任、被收窄的权利、被蚀出的牙釉质与缩小的领先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: surf hollowing the base of a cliff while the grass above moves inland.
core.cn: 核心意象：浪把崖脚掏空，上方的草地向内陆移动。

branches.en: ACT AND BE ACTED ON: the same verb works with an agent or with the surface itself.
branches.cn: 作用与受作用：同一动词既可带施事，也可描述表面本身。

branches.en: CUTTING DOWN: a river erodes a gorge by removing bed and bank.
branches.cn: 向下切割：河流靠移除河床与河岸切出峡谷。

branches.en: CHEMICAL TOOTH: acid erodes enamel by the same logic at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 化学的牙齿：酸在更小尺度上按同一逻辑侵蚀牙釉质。

branches.en: MONEY AND TRUST: costs and delays remove value the way water removes rock.
branches.cn: 金钱与信任：成本与延误会像水搬走岩石那样搬走价值。

branches.en: RIGHTS AND LEADS: small steps remove what was once solid.
branches.cn: 权利与领先：小步侵蚀移除曾经稳固之物。

intro.en: Erode is a Latin verb whose prefix and root both recur, and whose English family is unusually large.
intro.cn: erode 是拉丁动词，前缀与词根都反复出现，其英语词族异常庞大。

latinIntro.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' gives erode, erosion, corrode, erase and rodent; e- 'out' marks removal.
latinIntro.cn: rodere「啃」衍生 erode、erosion、corrode、erase 与 rodent；e-「出」标记移除。

items.example: The prefix marks taking something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记把某物取出。

items.example: The eroding bank threatens the road.
items.exampleCN: 正在侵蚀的河岸威胁道路。

definition_zh: 侵蚀的；由侵蚀形成的；与侵蚀作用有关的
definition_en: relating to erosion, or produced by the wearing away of rock and soil
core_image: 高原边缘，风把表层细土吹走，露出下面凹凸不平的岩面与浅沟
scene: 高原边缘，风把表层细土吹走，露出下面凹凸不平的岩面。The erosional surface beneath the soil is uneven and grooved.
sceneCN: 这里 erosional 指「由侵蚀作用形成的、侵蚀成的」（第 2 个义项：侵蚀成因的，尤指地形与岩面）；句意为土层之下的侵蚀面凹凸不平、布满浅沟。可辨识物件：高原边缘、被吹走的细土、裸露岩面、浅沟。

senses.title: Relating to erosion
senses.definition: of or concerning the process of erosion
senses.definitionCN: 指与侵蚀过程有关的
senses.example: The erosional history of the valley is read from its terraces.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河谷的侵蚀史可以从阶地读出。
senses.why: -al means 'relating to', so the adjective simply attaches to the process.
senses.whyCN: -al 意为「与……有关的」，因此这个形容词只是与过程相连。

senses.title: Produced by erosion
senses.definition: of a feature: shaped or cut by erosion
senses.definitionCN: 指由侵蚀塑造或切出的地形或特征
senses.example: The erosional surface beneath the soil is uneven and grooved.
senses.exampleCN: 土层之下的侵蚀面凹凸不平、布满浅沟。
senses.why: Features shaped by removal are called erosional to distinguish them from depositional ones.
senses.whyCN: 由移除塑造的地形称为侵蚀的，以区别于沉积形成的。

senses.title: Erosional surface
senses.definition: a surface cut into older rock and later buried by younger deposits
senses.definitionCN: 指切入较老岩石、后来被较新沉积覆盖的面
senses.example: The erosional surface marks a long pause in deposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个侵蚀面标记着沉积的一次长期间断。
senses.why: A surface cut into older rock is the clearest physical record of erosion.
senses.whyCN: 切入较老岩石的面是侵蚀最清楚的物证。

senses.title: Erosional unconformity or gap
senses.definition: a break in the rock record where erosion removed the missing layers
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石记录中因侵蚀移除若干层而形成的间断
senses.example: An erosional gap of fifty million years separates the beds.
senses.exampleCN: 两套岩层之间隔着一个五千万年的侵蚀间断。
senses.why: When the cut surface is buried, the missing layers become an unconformity.
senses.whyCN: 当切出的面被埋住，缺失的层就成为不整合。

senses.title: Erosional cycle
senses.definition: a cycle of uplift, downcutting and later flattening in a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 指地貌中抬升、下切与后期夷平的循环
senses.example: The erosional cycle ends on a broad plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这个侵蚀旋回终止于一片宽阔平原。
senses.why: A cycle is a long sequence of erosion steps, and the adjective names its products.
senses.whyCN: 旋回是一长串侵蚀步骤，形容词命名的是它的产物。

senses.title: Erosional remnant
senses.definition: an isolated hill or mass left standing after the surrounding rock was removed
senses.definitionCN: 指周围岩体被移除后残留的孤立丘体
senses.example: The butte is an erosional remnant of a harder layer.
senses.exampleCN: 这座孤山是较硬岩层的侵蚀残丘。
senses.why: A remnant is what erosion failed to remove.
senses.whyCN: 残丘是侵蚀没能移除的部分。

senses.title: Erosional plain or plateau
senses.definition: a surface reduced to near flatness chiefly by erosion
senses.definitionCN: 指主要由侵蚀削低到近于平坦的面
senses.example: The erosional plain stretches to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 这片侵蚀平原一直延伸到地平线。
senses.why: A plain is what erosion makes when it has finished its work.
senses.whyCN: 平原是侵蚀完成工作后造出的形态。

senses.title: Erosional valley or feature
senses.definition: a valley or shape cut by running water, ice or wind
senses.definitionCN: 指由流水、冰或风切出的谷或形状
senses.example: The erosional valley narrows to a gorge upstream.
senses.exampleCN: 这条侵蚀谷向上游收窄成峡谷。
senses.why: A valley is a cut feature, the everyday example of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 谷是被切出的地形，是这个形容词最日常的例子。

intro.en: Erosional is erosion with the Latin adjective ending -al, a form coined for geological writing in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: erosional 是 erosion 加拉丁形容词词尾 -al，是十九世纪地质写作中造出的形式。

items.en: Rodere 'to gnaw' underlies the whole family; its deeper origin is uncertain, and purported Indo-European links are reconstructions.
items.cn: rodere「啃」支撑整个词族；它更深的来源不确定，所声称的印欧关联均属重构。

items.en: E- 'out' plus rodere gave erodere, and the action noun erosio gave English erosion.
items.cn: e-「出」加 rodere 构成 erodere，动作名词 erosio 构成英语 erosion。

items.en: Latin -alis 'relating to' gives English -al, as in tidal and fluvial, so erosional means 'relating to erosion'.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis「与……有关的」构成英语 -al，如 tidal 与 fluvial，因此 erosional 意为「与侵蚀有关的」。

items.en: Geologists needed an adjective for surfaces and landforms cut by erosion and coined erosional alongside erosive, which describes the agent.
items.cn: 地质学家需要形容被侵蚀切出的面与地形的形容词，于是造出 erosional，与描述营力的 erosive 并列。

items.en: Erosional surface, erosional unconformity and erosional remnant became standard phrases in stratigraphy and geomorphology.
items.cn: 侵蚀面、侵蚀不整合与侵蚀残丘成为地层学与地貌学的标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the adjective's coinage date is not precisely recorded, and the deeper root of rodere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：该形容词的造词年代没有精确记录，rodere 的更深词根亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that resemble erosional; group two holds adjectives describing surfaces and processes in the same reports.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似 erosional 的形容词；第二组是同类报告中描述表面与过程的形容词。

entries.definition: Describes the force that does the eroding, as in erosive rainfall; erosional describes what the force leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 描述造成侵蚀的营力，如侵蚀性降雨；erosional 描述营力留下的结果。

entries.definition: The process itself; erosional is the adjective formed on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；erosional 是在其上构成的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to corrasion, the scraping of a bed by moving sediment, from com- plus radere 'scrape'; a near neighbour with another root.
entries.definitionCN: 指磨蚀作用，即运动沉积物对河床的刮磨，来自 com- 加 radere「刮」；词根不同的近邻。

entries.definition: Relating to chemical corrosion, from cor- plus rodere; it shares the rodere root but names chemical attack, not landscape cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学腐蚀，来自 cor- 加 rodere；共享 rodere 词根，却命名化学侵蚀而非地貌切割。

entries.definition: Describes surfaces and landforms built up by deposition; it is the standard counterpart of erosional.
entries.definitionCN: 指由沉积建造的面与地形；它是 erosional 的标准对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to the lowering of land by wearing away; it is close to erosional but stresses the loss of height.
entries.definitionCN: 指陆地因磨蚀而降低；与 erosional 接近，但强调高度的损失。

entries.definition: Relating to the stripping of soil and rock cover; it overlaps with erosional but emphasizes exposure.
entries.definitionCN: 指剥离土壤与岩石覆盖；与 erosional 重叠，但强调暴露。

entries.definition: Relating to wear by rubbing, as by sand; it is one mechanism within erosional landscapes.
entries.definitionCN: 指由摩擦造成的磨损，如砂磨；它是侵蚀地形中的一种机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain, the real stratigraphic phrases and the real contrast with erosive.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链、真实的地层说法与与 erosive 的真实对比。

normal.en: Erosion plus -al: 'relating to erosion', like tidal from tide and fluvial from river.
normal.cn: erosion 加 -al：「与侵蚀有关的」，如 tidal 来自 tide、fluvial 来自河流。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: erosional surface, erosional unconformity, erosional remnant, erosional cycle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：侵蚀面、侵蚀不整合、侵蚀残丘、侵蚀旋回。

normal.en: Keep erosive for the agent and erosional for the result.
normal.cn: erosive 留给营力，erosional 留给结果。

normal.en: The family runs erode, erosion, erosive, erosional, erodible.
normal.cn: 词族包括 erode、erosion、erosive、erosional、erodible。

normal.en: An erosional surface means missing time: the record was cut away, not added to.
normal.cn: 侵蚀面意味着缺失的时间：记录被切走，而不是被加上。

abstract.en: Picture a page with a hole in it where a chapter used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上有个洞，原本是一章。

abstract.en: Picture a hill that is the last leftover of a whole plateau.
abstract.cn: 想象一座山丘是整片高原的最后残余。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase cut by water instead of built by hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一段由水切出而非手工砌成的阶梯。

examples.en: The erosional surface separates two completely different faunas.
examples.cn: 这个侵蚀面把两个完全不同的动物群分开。

examples.en: An erosional remnant of limestone rises above the plain.
examples.cn: 一座石灰岩侵蚀残丘耸立在平原之上。

examples.en: The erosional cycle begins with uplift and ends with a peneplain.
examples.cn: 侵蚀旋回以抬升开始，以准平原结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一揉（ero）神（sion）闹（al）」——被揉掉之后留下的 → 侵蚀形成的

root: erosion（拉丁 e-「出」+ rodere「啃」+ -io）+ -al（拉丁 -alis「与……有关的」）→ erosional「侵蚀的、侵蚀形成的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective through geology: the process, the surface it cuts, the gap it leaves, the cycle it completes, the remnant it spares and the plain it finally makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个形容词穿过地质学：过程、它切出的面、它留下的间断、它完成的旋回、它保住的残丘，以及它最终造出的平原。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare grooved rock face where soil has just been stripped away.
core.cn: 核心意象：表土刚被剥去、露出沟槽的裸岩面。

branches.en: THE PROCESS NAMED: the adjective simply marks what belongs to erosion.
branches.cn: 命名过程：这个形容词只标记属于侵蚀的东西。

branches.en: WHAT IS LEFT: a grooved surface and a cut valley are both shaped by removal.
branches.cn: 留下的东西：沟槽面与被切出的谷都由移除塑造。

branches.en: SURFACE AND GAP: a cut surface, once buried, becomes a break in the record.
branches.cn: 面与间断：切出的面一旦被埋，就成为记录中的断口。

branches.en: CYCLE AND REMNANT: a cycle wears a landscape down and leaves isolated survivors.
branches.cn: 旋回与残丘：旋回把地貌削低，留下孤立的幸存者。

branches.en: THE PLAIN: at the end of the cycle, erosion produces flatness rather than height.
branches.cn: 平原：旋回结束时，侵蚀造出平坦而非高度。

intro.en: Erosional is a Latin noun of action with a Latin relational adjective ending, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: erosional 是拉丁动作名词加拉丁关系形容词词尾，两部分都可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin erosio 'a gnawing away' supplies the base; -alis 'relating to' supplies the ending, as in fluvialis and tidal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 erosio「啃蚀」提供词基；-alis「与……有关的」提供词尾，如 fluvialis 与 tidal。

items.example: The root names the wearing action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名磨蚀动作。
tidal 意为与潮汐有关的。
